descriptionAr: Why Cloud Infrastructure at Langfuse Your work will keep Langfuse running — everywhere. Langfuse processes over a billion trace events per month. When a Fortune 50 company relies on Langfuse in production, they're relying on the infrastructure you operate. You'll own uptime, performance, and cost efficiency across our entire cloud footprint — and you'll make sure every self-hosted deployment runs just as smoothly. You'll operate Langfuse Cloud on AWS ECS Fargate and ClickHouse Cloud, with Datadog as the observability backbone. You'll also own our public self-hosted infrastructure — including our Helm chart, Docker Compose setup, and everything in between — so that teams from startups to enterprises can run Langfuse on their own terms. This isn't a "maintain what exists" role. We're scaling fast, and you'll be the person who makes sure the infrastructure grows ahead of demand — not behind it. Langfuse is now part of ClickHouse, which means the team behind the database at the core of our stack is one channel away. Few infrastructure roles give you that kind of direct access to the people who build your most critical dependency. You will grow at Langfuse by Own Langfuse Cloud operations: You'll run our production environments on AWS ECS Fargate and ClickHouse Cloud. You'll manage deployments, autoscaling, capacity planning, and cost optimization — making sure we stay fast and affordable as traffic scales. Build world-class observability: You'll own our Datadog setup end to end — dashboards, alerts, and SLOs. When something degrades, you'll ensure we know before our customers do. You'll build the monitoring culture that lets the whole team ship with confidence. Make self-hosting effortless: Thousands of teams run Langfuse on their own infrastructure. You'll own and evolve our Helm chart, Docker Compose configuration, and deployment documentation. You'll turn "works on my machine" into "works on every machine" — from a single-node setup to a multi-region enterprise deployment. Automate everything: CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure-as-code, automated scaling, zero-downtime deployments. You'll replace manual processes with automation that makes the team faster and the platform more reliable. Scale for what's next: We're growing fast and new product directions — like complex long-running agent observability and real-time evaluation — push the infrastructure in new ways. You'll be thinking ahead about what breaks at 10x scale and building the foundation before we get there. 10x is always just one quarter away here at Langfuse. Harden security and compliance: As more enterprises adopt Langfuse, you'll help ensure our cloud and self-hosted deployments meet the security and compliance bar that large organizations require. What we're looking for Strong infrastructure or SRE engineer who gets excited about running systems at scale and making them better every day Experience operating production workloads on AWS (ECS/Fargate, networking, IAM, S3, etc.) or on comparable hyperscale vendors. Comfortable with container orchestration — Kubernetes and/or ECS, Helm charts, Docker Experience with infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, Pulumi, CloudFormation, or similar) Strong monitoring and observability instincts — you've built dashboards and alerts that actually caught problems (Datadog experience is a plus) You organize yourself. You have strong opinions about reliability, automation, and how to ship infrastructure changes safely Interest in open source software and genuine enjoyment helping users debug their self-hosted deployments Thrives in a small, accountable team where your output is visible and matters CS or quantitative degree preferred Bonus points: Experience with ClickHouse Cloud or other managed analytical databases Background in operating high-throughput event processing or observability infrastructure Contributions to open source infrastructure tooling (Helm charts, Terraform modules, etc.) Former founder Perks Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. We currently operate in over 25 countries. Healthcare - Employer contributions towards your healthcare. Equity in the company - Every new team member who joins our company receives stock options. Time off - Flexible time off in the US, generous entitlement in other countries. A USD$500 Home office setup if you’re a remote employee. Global Gatherings – We believe in the power of in-person connection and offer opportunities to engage with colleagues at company-wide offsites. Culture - We All Shape It As part of a rapidly scaling start-up, you will be instrumental in shaping our culture. Are you interested in finding out more about our culture? Learn more about our values here . Check out our blog posts or follow us on LinkedIn to find out more about what’s happening at ClickHouse. Equal Opportunity & Privacy ClickHouse provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type based on factors such as race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws. descriptionAr: Die Cartonplast Holding GmbH ist ein führender internationaler Anbieter von wiederverwendbaren Transportverpackungen für die Lebensmittel-, Getränke-, Pharma- und Industriebranche. Entwicklung und Präsentation kundenorientierter Lösungen, insbesondere in den Bereichen Kostenoptimierung, Prozessverbesserung und nachhaltige Verpackungslösungen. Enge Zusammenarbeit mit lokalen Geschäftsführern und internationalen Kollegen sowie regelmäßige Berichterstattung über Kundenaktivitäten, Geschäftspotenziale und Vertriebsfortschritte. descriptionAr: About Us At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company. At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in. The role of every seller at Cloudflare is to bring critical thinking, judgment, and trust to customer relationships and outcomes. You are the kind of operator who uses AI as a force multiplier every day, cares more about customer outcomes than job boundaries, and demonstrates curiosity, judgment, and high agency. Responsibilities Own and execute a comprehensive territory plan to consistently achieve and exceed sales and revenue targets. Cultivate long-term strategic relationships with key accounts and partners. Lead executive-level transformation narratives that earn the right to be in the architecture conversation. Leverage top partners as an extension of the sales team to co-sell alongside where they bring customer relationships, services capability, or procurement leverage. Drive regular forecast & pipeline cadences with top partners. Understand customer network architectures, the problems that Cloudflare can solve and effectively translate Cloudflare’s solutions to drive successful platform sales, ensuring clients can secure and scale their own AI-driven workloads. Manage contract negotiations and structure platform-level commercial commitments (multi-year, multi-product, outcome-anchored) rather than point-product deals. Stay engaged through onboarding, adoption, and the first renewal. Partner with Customer Engineers, Professional Services on a deployment plan with milestones tied to measurable outcomes. Proactively build and manage a robust sales pipeline by leveraging internal tools, AI-assisted research and pipeline sources (BDR, Channel, Marketing). Proficient in discovery, positioning, competitive selling, negotiation, closing, and multi-threaded land and expand strategies. Strong understanding of computer networking, cloud security technology, and how enterprise infrastructure adapts to automated data workflows. Exceptional interpersonal communication skills and value selling skills. Proficiency in modern sales software, customer data environments, and core systems (e.g., Salesforce, Tableau, G-suite). Thinks critically rather than reacting, exercises judgment under uncertainty, names risks honestly, shows genuine empathy for customers as people, can point to relationships built over time on trust, and demonstrates visible curiosity in how they prepare, sell, and learn. Willingness to actively engage with AI tools and experiment. Ability to travel as required. Cultural fluency for assigned markets; language proficiency where required. What Makes Cloudflare Special? descriptionAr: SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars. SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next. About the role We’re hiring the first AI Deployment Manager to partner with some of our most strategic enterprise customers. As an AI Deployment Manager, you’ll drive adoption, deliver measurable business value, and help shape how AI transforms engineering teams. You’ll act as the connective tissue between customer stakeholders and our internal teams, influencing both the Grok roadmap and each customer’s implementation strategy. This role is highly cross‑functional and customer‑facing. You understand software development workflows, care deeply about developer tools, and love helping engineering organizations succeed at scale. What you'll do Build and grow deep relationships with engineering leaders and power users at key accounts Partner with Field Engineering and Sales to deliver a seamless post‑sale experience Drive adoption of Grok by aligning usage with business objectives and engineering goals Guide customers on best practices for rollout, prompt strategy, context configuration, and internal enablement Serve as the customer’s voice internally and influence roadmap priorities Provide strategic account planning and regular business reviews with VP‑ and CTO‑level stakeholders Monitor account health, usage patterns, and product engagement to drive renewals and expansion You may be a fit if You have strong communication skills and executive presence, and are comfortable whiteboarding with developers and pivoting to value with a CTO You have a deep understanding of the software development lifecycle and engineering org structures You are fluent in technical workflows, AI tooling, and developer productivity (even if you haven’t been a full‑time engineer) You are customer‑obsessed with a knack for strategic thinking and problem‑solving You thrive in a startup environment: scrappy, proactive, and adaptable You have experience in TAM, Solutions Architecture, Customer Success, or Consulting for enterprise software About Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truthseeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code. Applying If there appears to be a fit, we'll reach to schedule 2-3 short technicals. After, we'll schedule an onsite in our office, where you'll work on a small project, discuss ideas, and meet the team.

descriptionAr: GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster. The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software. * Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab. An overview of this role As an Engineering Manager , you’ll guide GitLab’s dedicated Software Supply Chain Security (SSCS) Add-On engineering team as it develops core capabilities including Dependency Firewall, Build Provenance, Malicious Packages detection, and Artifact Signing . This is a founding management role where you’ll help shape how the team works, partner closely with the Staff Backend Engineer, Product Manager, and SSCS stage management, and turn a defined roadmap into steady, high-quality delivery for enterprise customers with strict security and compliance needs. You’ll focus on developing the team, creating a healthy operating rhythm, and establishing predictable execution for the SSCS SKU. You’ll join a product area where customers in regulated industries are already validating the need, and your work will help GitLab deliver software supply chain security features that customers can rely on. While technical credibility matters, your main focus will be growing a strong backend engineering team, enabling team members in their development, and creating the conditions for long-term delivery and quality. What you’ll do Guide a backend engineering team building the SSCS Add-On across dependency enforcement, build provenance, malicious package detection, and artifact signing. Be responsible for Drive engineering delivery for general availability milestones by aligning sequencing, scope, and dependencies with the Staff Backend Engineer and Product Manager. Develop the team by partnering with Talent Acquisition on sourcing, interview design, candidate evaluation, and hiring decisions. Run regular 1:1s, performance reviews, and career development conversations that enable growth and clear expectations. Advance engineering quality by monitoring cycle time, defect rates, and test coverage, and by addressing risks early. Coordinate quarterly planning and roadmap tradeoff discussions with SSCS stage leadership and Product. Work with Finance and other partners on headcount pacing and team planning as the Add-On scales. Represent the SSCS Add-On team within stage leadership discussions and help ensure strong communication across functions. What you’ll bring Over 3 years of experience guiding backend product engineering teams in security, DevOps, or platform engineering environments. Ability to hire and grow backend or security engineers in distributed team environments, with practical understanding of the talent landscape for these roles. Technical credibility to contribute to architecture discussions involving package registries, CI/CD pipeline security, and signing infrastructure. Experience managing predictable delivery across multi-quarter product roadmaps and managing cross-team dependencies. Comfort working in an asynchronous, documentation-driven organization with clear written communication. Familiarity with supply chain security, artifact management, or compliance-focused product areas, or transferable experience from related domains. Working knowledge of concepts related to frameworks and ecosystems such as SLSA and Sigstore. Ability to build credibility with engineers, product partners, and customer-facing stakeholders through clear judgment, coaching, and teamwork. About the team The SSCS Add-On team is a product engineering team within GitLab’s Software Supply Chain Security stage. We work on key capabilities in the SSCS Add-On SKU and collaborate closely with product and engineering partners to deliver security features for customers operating in regulated environments. You’ll report to the SSCS Senior Engineering Manager and partner directly with the Staff Backend Engineer and Product Manager. As a distributed team working asynchronously across regions, we are focused on strong delivery practices, team health, and scaling the product area with clarity and accountability. For more on how related teams work, see Team Handbook Page . descriptionAr: About the Team OpenAI is a frontier AI research and deployment company. Frontier research is at the center of how we advance our mission, with researchers, engineers, product leaders, operators, and many other teams working together to turn new capabilities into systems that benefit humanity. The People team helps OpenAI attract, engage, and support the exceptional talent this work requires. Employer Brand sits at the intersection of Research, Recruiting, Communications, Marketing, and Brand. Its mandate is to establish OpenAI in the talent market as a frontier research lab and make our distinctive research environment, mission, culture, and opportunity for impact relevant and tangible to every priority talent audience. About the Role We’re hiring an employer brand professional to bring OpenAI’s talent narrative to life through compelling content, communications, and social media. Reporting to the Employer Brand Manager, you’ll help translate our employer brand strategy into stories and campaigns that help candidates understand our work, our people, and the opportunity to contribute to our mission. This is a hands-on individual contributor role with broad employer brand responsibilities and a particular focus on writing, content planning, digital, and social storytelling. You’ll develop content that reflects the experiences of our researchers and employees, adapt stories for different audiences and channels, and help deliver a consistent, credible candidate experience. You’ll work closely with Recruiting, Marketing & Brand, Internal Communications, the broader People team, employees, hiring managers, and external partners to bring projects from idea through publication and measurement. In this role, you will: Develop and execute employer brand content and campaigns that bring OpenAI’s mission, culture, and work to life for priority talent audiences throughthru owned, earned, and paid content.our owned. Manage the day-to-day employer brand content calendar, coordinating social content, publishing, reviews, and deadlines with channel owners and cross-functional partners. Write and edit social posts, employee stories, careers content, recruiting communications, and other materials that help candidates understand why OpenAI. Identify story opportunities and work with researchers, employees, and hiring teams to turn their experiences into accurate, engaging content across written, visual, and video formats. Partner with Communications and Marketing & Brand to adapt content for social channels, maintain a consistent voice, and test formats that resonate with talent audiences. Support broader employer brand initiatives, including recruiting events, candidate communications, and resources for recruiters and hiring managers. Coordinate content production and review workflows, keeping source materials, permissions, approvals, and project information organized and current. Flag outdated or inconsistent information and escalate sensitive reviews or delivery risks. Track content and campaign performance, gather audience feedback, and use those insights to improve future work, distinguishing observed results from interpretation. Handle sensitive information and employee and candidate stories with care, ensuring accuracy, appropriate approvals, and respect for consent. Project manager for key employer brand projects with the ability to work with cross functional stakeholders. You might thrive in this role if you: Have 10+ years of experience in employer brand, communications, social media, marketing, recruiting, content, events, or a related field. Are a strong writer and editor who can turn complex information into clear, credible stories while preserving accuracy and nuance. Have experience creating or coordinating content for social channels and understand how to adapt messaging and formats for different audiences. Can manage content projects from brief through delivery, balancing creative work with organization, follow-through, and attention to detail. Build productive relationships across teams and are comfortable gathering input, coordinating reviews, and managing multiple deadlines. Approach employee and candidate stories with discretion, respect for consent, and care for the people represented. Are comfortable using content management, social publishing, spreadsheet, and presentation tools, and are willing to learn new platforms. Are curious about technical work and talent audiences, ask thoughtful questions, and enjoy learning from subject-matter experts. Use feedback and performance data to improve your work, and are thoughtful about using AI tools while maintaining human judgment, accuracy, and confidentiality. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. descriptionAr: About the Team OpenAI's Global Network Infrastructure team is responsible for building and operating the global network backbone that connects our rapidly expanding compute infrastructure. Our work enables reliable, high-performance connectivity across data centers, cloud service providers, and network points of presence (PoPs), supporting the infrastructure behind OpenAI's research and products. As OpenAI continues to scale its compute footprint globally, we are expanding our network infrastructure to meet increasing demands for capacity, reliability, and operational efficiency. Our team works across physical network design, carrier connectivity, network deployment, and operational troubleshooting to deliver resilient infrastructure at exceptional scale. About the Role We are looking for a hands-on Network Infrastructure Engineer to help design, deploy, activate, and operate OpenAI's global wide area network (WAN) infrastructure. In this role, you will take direct ownership of bringing new network connectivity online, working closely with fiber providers, cloud service providers, and internal infrastructure teams to establish reliable connectivity across our global backbone. You will be involved in everything from physical network design and circuit provisioning to troubleshooting complex connectivity issues across Layer 1, Layer 2, and Layer 3. You will play a critical role in expanding our network footprint, bringing new PoPs online, and ensuring that our infrastructure operates reliably as OpenAI continues to grow. We're looking for engineers who enjoy working close to the infrastructure, thrive on solving difficult networking problems, and bring an automation-first mindset to scaling network operations. In This Role, You Will: Design, deploy, and support WAN infrastructure across data centers, network PoPs, and cloud connectivity environments. Own the end-to-end activation and turn-up of network circuits, working directly with fiber carriers and cloud service providers to establish and validate connectivity. Troubleshoot complex network issues across physical, Layer 2, and Layer 3 infrastructure, including optical signal problems, FEC errors, routing issues, and connectivity failures. Diagnose and isolate network failures across carrier, cloud provider, and internal infrastructure boundaries, driving issues through resolution. Contribute to physical network infrastructure design, including port mappings, fiber and cable layouts, optical distribution frames (ODFs), and connectivity planning. Monitor network health, circuit utilization, and performance to proactively identify capacity constraints and reliability risks. Build automation and tooling to streamline network provisioning, deployment validation, troubleshooting, and operational workflows. Collaborate with network engineering, data center infrastructure, and external service providers to support the expansion of OpenAI's global backbone. descriptionAr: About the Team The IP Infrastructure team builds and operates the systems that enable OpenAI to share research and engineering technology securely and reliably with strategic partners. Our work spans continuously running pipelines for model weights, configurations, code, and container images. We work closely with research, security, developer infrastructure, and partner engineering teams to turn complex requirements into dependable software. We’re a small, collaborative team with direct ownership of systems that support important partnerships. About the Role We’re looking for a software engineer to build and improve the backend services behind these workflows. You’ll work primarily in Python, take projects from design through production, and make our systems more reliable and easier to operate as partner integrations evolve. The work combines hands-on engineering with careful judgment. You’ll translate requirements about what can be shared into clear, testable business logic, debug problems across system boundaries, and collaborate with the teams that build and use the underlying infrastructure. This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week. In this role, you will: Build and maintain automated pipelines that transfer model weights, configurations, code, and container images between OpenAI and partner environments Implement the validation and business logic that determines how artifacts are prepared and shared Improve production reliability through testing, monitoring, useful diagnostics, and robust failure handling Integrate services with source control, object storage, and build and container tooling, working closely with the owners of shared infrastructure Partner with researchers, security teams, and external engineers to understand requirements and resolve integration problems Improve existing workflows and use AI tools where they can make the systems we build more effective You might thrive in this role if you: Have strong Python skills and experience building, testing, and debugging backend software Have taken a service, pipeline, or automation project from implementation into production and helped keep it reliable Enjoy investigating how systems fit together and tracing problems across services and dependencies Can turn ambiguous requirements into practical software while exercising sound judgment around sensitive information Communicate clearly with technical and nontechnical collaborators and enjoy working with partner engineering teams Learn unfamiliar systems quickly and take responsibility for following problems through to resolution Experience with cloud services, object storage, containers, or CI/CD is helpful. descriptionAr: About the Team The B2B Content team helps business audiences understand what AI makes possible and how to put it to work. We develop narrative, editorial, demo, and adoption programs that connect OpenAI’s products to concrete business value. We partner closely with Product Marketing, Demand Generation, Customer Education, Sales, and other teams to create content that is useful on its own and supports the broader customer journey. We value people who are eager to learn, have a bias for action, and look beyond the immediate deliverable. We build the tools, systems, and shared practices that help the whole team produce better work over time. About the Role We’re looking for a Product Content Creator to help create the next generation of AI-native marketing content. You’ll develop videos, interactive tutorials, live demos, written guides, and other experiences that help business audiences understand what AI makes possible and how it applies to their work. This is a hands-on creative role spanning demand generation and product adoption. You’ll explore product capabilities, build and test workflows, and produce content for campaigns that introduce people to useful ideas and help them put those ideas into practice. You’ll maintain evergreen campaign content and develop new adoption campaigns, using practical workflows, research, and thought leadership as source material. You’ll use Codex and other AI tools to prototype ideas and create experiences that would previously have required a larger production team. We’re looking for the fluency of a coding-assistant power user; an engineering background isn’t required. Strong judgment about the idea, the audience, and the finished experience matters as much as the ability to build it. You’ll partner with Product Marketing on positioning and product accuracy, Demand Generation on campaign goals and distribution needs, and Demo Studio on demonstrations and production. You’ll own the content from concept through delivery, choosing the format that best serves the idea and the audience. This is an individual-contributor role for someone who enjoys making, explaining, experimenting, and shipping. The role is hybrid and will be based in San Francisco, Monday through Wednesday. Thursday and Friday are work-from-home days, with occasional in-office attendance as needed for live webinars. In this role, you will: Develop creative concepts and produce content for Demand Generation campaigns, grounded in audience needs, product workflows, research, and expert perspectives. Personally create videos, interactive tutorials, live demos, and written guides, carrying work from the initial idea through a finished asset. Use Codex and other AI tools to build and test workflows, prototype interactive experiences, and improve how content is produced. Develop and test original content formats, learn from audience response, and turn the strongest ideas into recurring series or reusable campaign experiences. Choose formats for what they help the audience understand or do. Develop webinar content with the webinar strategist, including the storyline, presentation, demonstration, and useful follow-up resources. Work with Product Marketing, subject-matter experts, and Demo Studio to make content accurate, substantive, and engaging. Work with customer-facing teams to learn how people actually use the products, where they get stuck, and which workflows are worth demonstrating. Use those insights to develop relevant stories and adoption content. Adapt strong ideas across formats and audiences while giving each asset a clear purpose within the campaign. Deliver usable campaign assets to Demand Generation, with clear audience framing, supporting copy, and a proposed next action. Use audience feedback and campaign results with DG to improve the content, and keep reusable workflows, examples, and source material current. Maintain evergreen campaign content, updating workflows, demonstrations, and supporting resources as products and audience needs change. Create adoption campaign content that helps people try relevant workflows, overcome common difficulties, and continue using them in their work. Review campaign results and audience feedback with partners to understand both what attracts interest and what helps people successfully use the product. You might thrive in this role if you: Have a portfolio of substantive content you personally created across several formats, such as video, interactive tutorials, live demos, and written guides. Work projects, side projects, and experiments driven by your own curiosity are all relevant—we want to understand what you made and the decisions behind it. Are a confident user of Codex or comparable coding assistants and can show how you used them to build, test, and improve something useful. An engineering background isn’t required. Bring strong creative and editorial judgment: you can recognize an interesting idea, explain why a format works, and improve an experience beyond the first version. Can learn a product deeply enough to demonstrate real workflows and explain them clearly to business audiences with different levels of technical fluency. Write clearly, communicate well on video or in live demonstrations, and can turn complex material into something people want to spend time with. Understand how content supports marketing campaigns and can work with Demand Generation on audience needs, campaign goals, and what the results suggest changing. Take ownership from an ambiguous brief through delivery, balancing experimentation with the practical work required to ship. May have developed these skills in product marketing, developer relations, product education, creative technology, or content marketing. Relocation support is available for new hires. About the Role You will build and run OpenAI’s trade compliance program across Europe. Your remit spans cross-border shipping routes, partner and supplier arrangements, daily trade operations and compliance oversight for the legal entities involved. You will work with Legal, direct tax and indirect tax teams to design structures that meet trade requirements while improving cost and speed. Evaluate company, transaction, partner and supplier arrangements to improve cost, speed and operating reliability. Build the European trade compliance program and launch cross-border shipping routes. Put customs, import, export, sanctions and cross-border e-commerce requirements into workable processes. Own ongoing European import, export and returns operations, including customs warehousing where needed. Manage brokers and service providers, resolve issues and maintain reliable service as volume and complexity grow. Set and test compliance policies and controls for each legal entity. Maintain required authorizations, respond to rule changes, prepare for audits, resolve gaps and report risks to leaders. Personally manage relationships with customs and other trade authorities. Work with Legal to defend compliance positions and programs, respond to audits and inquiries, and resolve issues. Use AI to improve trade analysis, document review and ongoing monitoring. Build and test these processes, retain human review and decision records, and measure gains in accuracy and speed. Use shipment, inventory and customs data to investigate problems and compare options. Define the data and systems the program needs, and track whether processes and controls work. Bring business, supply chain, Finance, Tax, Legal and technology teams together to turn strategy into clear procedures, training and measurable operating improvements. You might thrive in this role if you have: Deep European customs expertise, including EU customs law, classification, valuation, origin and importer/exporter responsibilities. Practical experience applying different customs valuation methods and a working knowledge of import, export and sanctions requirements. A record of building trade programs from the ground up and making business decisions that balance compliance, cost, speed and operating needs, in partnership with Legal and Tax. Direct experience managing hardware imports and bonded warehouse compliance across multiple European countries. Personal responsibility for decisions, controls and ongoing operations. Experience personally managing regulatory relationships and defending compliance programs, positions and actions in reviews, audits or inquiries. Ability to investigate detailed data, question assumptions and recommend action. Practical experience using AI tools and checking their outputs. Sound judgment, personal accountability and clear communication when facts or requirements are uncertain; a relevant degree or equivalent practical experience. Experience managing trade compliance at the volume and complexity of a global supply chain. About the Role This is a hands-on software engineering role on the Cloudflare One Appliance team. You will shape and build the Linux-based edge runtime and distributed control plane that connect customer sites to Cloudflare. As a Senior Systems Engineer, you will work across low-level systems, distributed services, and API design while providing technical leadership for major initiatives. Our architecture follows a “light branch, heavy cloud” philosophy: policy and intelligence belong in Cloudflare’s network unless locality is required for correctness, survivability, performance, or user experience. You will use strong technical judgment to decide what belongs to the appliance and what belongs in the Cloudflare's network, building systems that are secure, observable, resilient to partial failures, and safe to operate across a large fleet carrying customer-critical traffic. Responsibilities Build systems end to end: Design and implement capabilities spanning the cloud control plane, Linux appliance runtime, telemetry pipeline, and physical, virtual, and cloud deployment environments. Build a Linux-based networking platform: Develop and harden the appliance dataplane. Build secure, reliable networking capabilities using technologies such as IPsec, MASQUE, eBPF, and Linux kernel networking primitives while keeping the system small, predictable, and secure. Engineer reliable fleet control: Build distributed control-plane and state-management systems that safely deliver configuration and commands, tolerate intermittent connectivity and partial failures, converge to known-good state, and support zero-touch operation across large device fleets. Secure the device lifecycle: Improve hardware-backed identity, attestation, secure boot, immutable operating-system images, credential rotation, and staged over-the-air upgrades with safe rollback and recovery. Make operability a product feature: Design telemetry, diagnostics, synthetic tests, support bundles, and remote operations that help customers and support teams understand the system without treating the appliance as a black box. Drive customer-centered product decisions: Work with customers, Product, Support, and Solutions Engineering to understand customer requirements and turn them into pragmatic technical direction. Bring clear opinions, and revise them when customer feedback or production evidence points to a better answer. Own production outcomes: Prototype quickly, ship in safe increments, and own rollout, monitoring, incident follow-up, and long-term maintainability. Lead across teams: Set architectural direction for major initiatives, write clear technical proposals, conduct rigorous reviews, and mentor other engineers. Build executable plans with Cloudflare WAN, Gateway, DEX, the Cloudflare One Client, and platform and security teams. Experience designing and implementing distributed control planes, desired-state reconciliation, remote configuration, or similar systems that manage large, intermittently connected fleets. Experience designing secure systems, including threat modeling, least privilege, credential handling, and software supply-chain integrity. A track record of owning ambiguous initiatives from discovery through production, including architecture, implementation, staged deployment, incident response, and failure analysis. descriptionAr: About the Team The Guardian team builds practical safety and oversight systems for increasingly capable AI agents. Our goal is to make it possible for agents to take on longer-running, higher-autonomy work while preserving meaningful safeguards, respecting user intent, and intervening when actions could cause serious or difficult-to-reverse harm. Auto-review is an early example of this work. When an agent reaches a permission boundary, a separate model evaluates the proposed action in context and determines whether it should proceed. The team is now extending this foundation into more capable oversight systems that account for richer user context, support a broader range of agent experiences, and integrate across OpenAI products. Guardian sits at the intersection of engineering, alignment research, product, infrastructure, and security. The team already has a strong engineering foundation in London and will continue to grow there as a concentrated, highly collaborative group. About the Role We are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead and grow the Guardian team in London. You will own the engineering strategy and execution for production systems that evaluate agent behavior, identify risk, and take appropriate action without creating unnecessary friction for users. This is a builder-manager role with substantial technical depth. You will set direction, develop engineers, and create the operating cadence for a high-performing team, while remaining close enough to the work to shape architecture, review designs, debug difficult problems, and write code when it is the highest-leverage way to help the team move forward. The role is highly visible and cross-functional. You will work closely with alignment researchers to translate emerging research into dependable systems, and with product teams to make agent safety a foundational capability across OpenAI. This role is based in our London office. In this role, you will Lead, hire, and develop a London-based team of engineers working across agent safety, backend systems, applied AI, and product infrastructure. Set the technical roadmap for Auto-review and the broader Guardian platform, balancing safety, product utility, latency, and operational reliability. Build production systems that evaluate agent actions in real time, detect potentially harmful behavior, and support safe recovery or escalation paths. Improve how oversight systems understand user intent, environmental context, permissions, and relevant personalization signals while protecting privacy and avoiding unnecessary friction. Partner closely with alignment researchers to turn prototypes, evaluations, and new monitoring techniques into scalable product capabilities. Work across Product, Security, Infrastructure, and other engineering teams to integrate Guardian capabilities into agent experiences throughout OpenAI. Establish rigorous evaluation and operational practices, including adversarial testing, failure analysis, monitoring, and metrics for safety performance, false positives, latency, and user impact. You might thrive in this role if you Have significant experience leading engineering teams that shipped complex, high-stakes production systems end to end. Have built with AI agents or large language models in a core product, startup, or technically serious independent project, and understand the unique challenges of agentic systems. Bring strong product-engineering judgment and can navigate tradeoffs across safety, usability, speed, and reliability. Can partner effectively with research teams, translate open-ended findings into engineering plans, and communicate clearly across technical disciplines. Have a thoughtful management system for hiring, coaching, performance, and execution. Care deeply about building AI systems that are useful, trustworthy, and safe. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. Improve session reliability, startup time, interactive latency, and resource efficiency; validate improvements with measurements. Write maintainable code, automated tests, and clear design notes; participate in constructive code and design reviews. Collaborate with teammates and partner teams, communicate trade-offs and blockers, and incorporate feedback. Ability to navigate an unfamiliar codebase, break a defined problem into deliverable steps, and test correctness and failure cases. A systematic approach to debugging and performance analysis, using evidence to form and test hypotheses. Clear communication, collaborative problem-solving, and a willingness to learn Rust, Go, TypeScript, and the rest of our stack. Bonus Points These are preferred qualifications, not prerequisites. Prior Browser Isolation or Cloudflare experience is not required. Browser engines, Chromium, browser sandboxing, or security-sensitive systems. Low-latency streaming, graphics, remote computing, or other real-time systems. Container and workload orchestration, including Nomad or Kubernetes, and service discovery. Experience using Rust for systems programming or distributed services. Go or TypeScript; WebRTC, Skia, WebAssembly, or WebGL. Production observability, capacity planning, incident response, or build and release infrastructure. descriptionAr: About the Team Cloud service providers give developers a way to use OpenAI models in the environments where they already build and run software. Our team works with Go-to-Market (GTM), Product, Engineering, and Finance to understand which customers we can reach through these providers and what helps them grow from a first API call to a production workload. About the Role In your first few months, you’ll identify a customer segment or workload where OpenAI can grow, recommend an investment to GTM, Product, and Engineering, and define how we’ll know whether it brought new usage to OpenAI. Your first priority will be to explain what drives usage and revenue across providers. You’ll use that understanding to help GTM decide which customers and workloads to invest in and to build forecasts the team can plan against. A customer might sign a substantial cloud commitment and send very little traffic. You can sit down with the account team, trace the customer’s first requests, and work out whether they need help launching, access to a different model, or more capacity. When you see the same opportunity across customers, your work can change where OpenAI invests. In This Role, You Will: Build a reliable view of the business from provider usage reports, billing records, and API logs. Show how new workloads, expansion, changes in price, and shifts in model mix contribute to growth. Estimate how much demand cloud distribution adds to OpenAI. Trace customer activity across channels to distinguish new use cases from traffic that moved from the direct API. Identify where customers are ready to scale. Combine what account teams hear with evidence on request failures, latency, and model availability. Work with Product and Engineering on a change and measure what happens to usage. Shape growth plans with GTM and Finance. Estimate what existing workloads and upcoming launches can contribute by year end, test the assumptions that matter most, and recommend where to focus with each provider. Own the consumption forecast. Compare forecasts with actual usage over the same period, explain the biggest misses, and use what you learn to improve the next forecast. You Might Thrive in This Role If You: Like questions that take you from a conversation with an account team to a query about a single API request. You’re curious about why a customer’s behavior differs from what the numbers first suggest. Are comfortable making a recommendation while some questions are still open. You can tell a sales leader where you’d invest and explain to an engineer what evidence would change your mind. Qualifications Experience independently leading data science work on a product, growth, or commercial question that changed a business decision. Strong SQL and Python skills. You can join incomplete datasets, choose the right unit of analysis, and validate an aggregate result against individual customers or workloads. Experience using cohorts, experiments, or observational comparisons to assess what drove a change. You can explain how customer selection affects the conclusion and evaluate a forecast against a simple baseline. Preferred Qualifications Experience with API platforms, cloud marketplaces, enterprise GTM, or a usage-based business. Experience connecting service reliability or capacity to customer adoption, or using demand forecasts to guide a commercial or infrastructure investment. descriptionAr: GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster. The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software. * Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab. An overview of this role As the Director, Strategic Partnerships, you will own GitLab's relationships with its two major cloud infrastructure partners: AWS and Google Cloud. This is a single-threaded owner role, reporting to the VP, Corporate Development & Strategic Partnerships. You will shape partnership strategy from the top down and drive execution from the ground up, this is as much about running the weekly grind of a partnership as it is about setting its direction, turning strategic relationships into durable business outcomes. You will own the commercial relationship end-to-end: managing GitLab's cloud infrastructure spend and consumption commitments, and leading renewal negotiations for enterprise agreements (e.g., EDPs, MACCs, or equivalent) before they come due. You will also own the technical and go-to-market side of each relationship: driving product integrations, shaping joint go-to-market strategy, and connecting GitLab's product roadmap and AI strategy to concrete partner initiatives. This is not a co-sell, channel, or revenue-through-partners role. Success here looks like disciplined commercial ownership, technical integration depth, and renewal outcomes that protect and grow GitLab's position, not partner-sourced pipeline or quota attainment. This role sits close to GitLab's evolving AI strategy and the future of our AI-powered DevSecOps platform. You will develop a clear point of view, represent these partnerships with senior stakeholders, and personally drive the day-to-day work that spans multi-year planning and weekly execution, chasing down blockers, keeping workstreams on track, and doing the detailed follow-through yourself rather than delegating it. What you'll do Serve as the primary owner and point of contact for GitLab's cloud infrastructure partnerships with AWS and Google Cloud, personally accountable for the direction, operating rhythm, and outcomes of each. Own the full commercial lifecycle of each relationship: negotiating rates and terms, tracking consumption against committed spend, and leading renewal negotiations well ahead of contract expiration. Manage cloud infrastructure spend as a standing responsibility, partnering with Finance/FinOps on forecasting, true-ups, and cost optimization across both hyperscalers. Drive product integrations with each partner, working directly with engineering and product management counterparts on both sides to identify, scope, and deliver joint technical initiatives. Develop and lead joint go-to-market strategy for each partnership, connecting GitLab's business priorities, product roadmap, and AI strategy to concrete partner initiatives, and then own getting those plans executed. Build strong working relationships across partner organizations, including executives, product management, engineering, sales, and marketing stakeholders. Run a disciplined operating cadence across complex initiatives, with clear priorities, owners, timelines, coordination points, and follow-through you drive yourself. Coordinate cross-functional work inside GitLab to support partnership goals, aligning teams across product, engineering, sales, marketing, finance, and the executive group. Translate partner opportunities and requests into actionable internal plans, including roadmap discussions, integration needs, commercial terms, and executive recommendations. Track and communicate measurable partnership outcomes such as spend efficiency, consumption trends, renewal terms secured, integration progress, and joint go-to-market execution. Represent the partnerships at the executive level by preparing clear recommendations, briefing executives, and helping drive alignment on investments, trade-offs, and next steps. What you'll bring Significant experience owning strategic partnerships, alliance relationships, or vendor/commercial relationships in enterprise software, cloud, and/or AI, with a track record of being in the details, not just setting direction. This experience should reflect owning one or a small number of relationships in depth, not administering a large multi-partner channel ecosystem. Direct experience managing enterprise cloud commercial agreements (e.g., EDP, MACC, or similar consumption/spend commitments) with at least one major hyperscaler, including experience owning a renewal cycle from expiration planning through negotiation and close. Experience driving product or technical integrations with a cloud partner, and shaping joint go-to-market strategy that connects a product roadmap to partner initiatives. Strong ownership mindset with the ability to operate as a single-threaded owner

descriptionAr: About Us At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company. At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in. Available Location: San Francisco, CA What you will do as a Customer Engineer The Customer Engineer (CE) is the core driver of our technical go-to-market strategy: a trusted technical advisor and primary architect of the customer journey. You will bridge the gap between technical strategy and business value—guiding enterprise clients from initial pre-sales technical validation through onboarding, deployment architecture, and full lifecycle expansion. Sitting within the GTM organization and reporting to a Customer Engineering Leader, you will not hand off your customers once an initial agreement is reached. Instead, you will operate as a quota-carrying technologist, leveraging AI-augmented workflows to eliminate administrative toil so you can focus on high-value architectural design and driving measurable business outcomes across the entire customer journey. Define, scope, success criteria, and technical evaluations plans for Proof of Concepts (PoCs) and Technical Validations. Deliver tailored technical presentations, architectural diagrams, and demonstrations that show how Cloudflare solves specific performance, security, and reliability challenges. Proactively address complex technical objections, security compliance questions, and edge-case architectural requirements during the sales cycle. Take accountability for a suitable solution deployment strategy (Customer, Partner or Cloudflare Professional services) being an integral part of all proposals. Customer Adoption & Value Realization: Provide oversight to technical onboarding and implementation, but not execute the implementation, serving as the primary executive and engineering contact for the customer. Design structured migration and onboarding blueprints tailored to the customer’s environment (e.g. DNS migrations, Zero Trust rollouts, WAF tuning guidance), and act as the lead consultant for customer engineering teams, walking them step-by-step through configuration best practices.  Partner with Account Executives to own discovery, demos, onboarding, technical health, risk, and expansion strategy. Proactively monitor customer health scores and telemetry to ensure rapid time-to-value, resolve integration bottlenecks, and reduce deployment risk. Commercial Accountability & Expansion: Carry a variable quota tied directly to new business acquisition and/or ongoing account growth. Be commercially accountable for ensuring deep platform adoption, retaining revenue, and identifying strategic cross-sell and up-sell opportunities based on product usage data. Lead technical Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) to translate platform capabilities into return on investment for C-level executives. Trusted Advisory: Act as a trusted technical advisor throughout the entire customer lifecycle, maintaining a continuous, deep relationship with key stakeholders from initial onboarding through maturity, renewal, and expansion. Provide thought partnership on architecture, AI control layers, security posture, and deployment confidence. Identify potential deployment risks or integration bottlenecks early, and provide remediation strategies to de-risk customer outcomes.  AI Orchestration & Workflow Automation: Leverage AI agents, Large Language Models (LLMs), and internal platforms to automate routine tasks such as RFP/Security Questionnaire responses, sandbox provisioning, basic telemetry monitoring, and internal/external documentation, reclaiming your time for strategic customer advisory. Education & Enablement: Partner closely with the Enablement Team to design, build, and govern technical resources. Define, document, and educate both internal teams and customers on deliverables such as Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), architectural best practices, and technical guides to continuously raise the technical baseline across the organization. descriptionAr: About the Team OpenAI’s Enterprise Go-To-Market organization helps the world’s largest companies adopt and scale our AI platform across their business, from ChatGPT Enterprise to our developer platform and APIs. We partner with organizations across Financial Services, Life Sciences, and Retail to build new AI-powered customer experiences, transform operations, and reimagine how work gets done in highly regulated and technically complex environments. As adoption accelerates through pilots, experimentation, and developer-led use cases, the GTM team turns that momentum into durable, enterprise-wide deployments. Business Development sits at the front of this motion, where technical curiosity turns into executive engagement, and early product signals become enterprise-wide deployments. About the Role This role is designed as a launchpad for future sellers at OpenAI. This is a highly strategic role with significant exposure to enterprise sales, product, and customer strategy. You’ll develop core skills in discovery, stakeholder mapping, deal shaping, and executive communication while building a deep understanding of how leading companies adopt AI. We are looking for individuals with 4-6+ years of professional experience (with 2-4 years of those in a full 360 sales closing role) who are motivated to grow into world-class enterprise sellers over time. While many individuals in this role go on to become Account Directors or take on broader GTM roles, progression is based on performance and business needs rather than a fixed timeline. For the right person, this is one of the most accelerated paths to break into sales at OpenAI and build a long-term career in AI go-to-market. In this role, you will identify, shape, and advance complex enterprise opportunities by turning product usage, pilots, and inbound demand into qualified, high-conviction enterprise opportunities for our Large Enterprise and Strategic Accounts teams. This role is based in our Dublin, Ireland office. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. Please note that fluency in English and French is required for this role. In this role, you will: Partner with Account Directors on account strategy, multi-threading, and deal progression Design and execute targeted Enterprise outbound strategies using industry context, stakeholder mapping, and product signal to break into priority accounts Lead high-quality discovery to uncover business priorities, map stakeholders, and assess enterprise readiness Contribute to pipeline reviews by sharing outbound activity, account insights, and early competitive signals. Build and iterate on AI-enabled GTM workflows (GPTs/agents) to scale prospecting and qualification You may thrive in this role if you: Have 4+ years of relevant experience in enterprise sales Have a track record of consistently hitting and exceeding ambitious targets in enterprise or strategic sales environments (share your attainment on your CV!) Experience selling into regulated or complex industries (Financial Services, Life Sciences, Retail) Strong communication skills and executive presence; able to build credibility with senior C-Suite stakeholders across an organisation, and speak fluently with technical buyers Strong interest and above average knowledge of the AI landscape with the ability to connect OpenAI products to real customer value and business outcomes You enjoy evangelizing new technology and helping the market understand what’s possible You’re comfortable with ambiguity, moving quickly, and operating well with a high degree of ownership About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. This team’s ethos is to support OpenAI’s mission and goals by clearly and authentically explaining our technology, values, and approach to safely building powerful AI. About the Role We’re looking for a senior communications leader to shape how OpenAI communicates about cybersecurity. This person will define the global narrative, lead communications for major product, research, and business milestones, and build sustained programs that explain how OpenAI is helping advance cyber defense while managing the risks created by increasingly capable models. The role will connect OpenAI’s work across cybersecurity products and capabilities, responsible deployment, threat intelligence, enterprise security, research, and public policy. You will work closely with Security, Product, Research, Preparedness, Safety, Global Affairs, Go-to-Market, Legal, and Marketing to anticipate opportunities and risks, develop coordinated communications, and build trust with security practitioners, customers, policymakers, and the public. This is both a strategic and hands-on role. The right person will be comfortable defining a long-term communications strategy, building the systems and relationships needed to execute it, and personally leading through major launches, technical disclosures, and fast-moving issues. This role reports to the Head of Communications, Business and is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days per week in the office and offer relocation assistance. In this role, you will: Define and lead communications strategy for OpenAI’s cybersecurity work, from global narrative development through launches, research, threat reporting, and sustained storytelling. Build a clear, differentiated story about how OpenAI can strengthen cyber defense while developing and deploying advanced capabilities responsibly. Lead communications for major cybersecurity products, model capabilities, research, partnerships, policy initiatives, and company milestones. Partner closely with the Product and Research Communications team, along with Security, Product, Research, Preparedness, Safety, Global Affairs, Go-to-Market, Legal, and Marketing, to deliver coordinated communications across earned, owned, executive, and social channels. Translate complex technical, security, product, and policy decisions into clear and credible communications, while establishing messaging systems and operating rhythms that keep teams aligned. You might thrive in this role, if you have: 12+ years of communications experience, with deep experience in cybersecurity, security technology, threat intelligence, national security, infrastructure, or another highly technical field. Strong press instincts and relationships, with a track record of shaping narratives and landing meaningful coverage with cybersecurity, technology, policy, or business media. descriptionAr: Replit is the agentic software creation platform that enables anyone to build applications using natural language. With millions of users worldwide, Replit is democratizing software development by removing traditional barriers to application creation. About the Role Replit enables people to build software with AI. The systems underneath that experience must support safe production changes, measurable reliability, and predictable performance as usage grows. This Engineering Manager will lead SRE across observability, incident management, load testing, performance engineering, cloud cost and capacity, and rollout infrastructure . You'll lead and grow an existing team that builds and operates production platforms and works hands-on across application and infrastructure boundaries. This is a software-building leadership role, not simply an incident-management function. You'll help teams ship safely, understand production behavior, and remove performance bottlenecks through concrete engineering improvements. You should be comfortable going deep on a rollout failure or performance investigation while developing technical leaders and sustainable ownership across a distributed team. What You'll Do Observability. Build and operate metrics, logs, traces, and alerting capabilities. Help teams establish meaningful SLOs and use production telemetry to diagnose problems and verify improvements. Incident Management. Own incident tooling and practices, coordinate cross-team response, and turn incident reviews into engineering improvements that reduce recovery time and repeat failures. Load Testing. Build and maintain load/failure testing capabilities. Validate critical paths under expected demand, quantify headroom, and test recovery and production readiness with service owners. Performance Engineering. Lead deep engagements with internal teams on SLOs and end-to-end performance. Use profiling, telemetry, and load tests to identify bottlenecks and deliver improvements with service owners—not just recommendations. Stay technically engaged. Review designs and production changes, debug difficult failure modes, and use AI coding tools—including Replit—to prototype and automate. Apply rigorous review and verification to AI-generated changes. Build and grow a high-ownership engineering team. Coach engineers, develop technical leaders, manage performance, and hire against agreed needs. Make distributed collaboration, mentoring, and backup coverage deliberate rather than relying on a few permanent escalation points. Measure outcomes and close the loop. Track rollout safety, recovery time, repeat incidents, critical-path latency/throughput, test coverage, and improvements arising from cost/capacity analysis. Agree success measures and continuing ownership with partner teams. What You'll Bring Demonstrated engineering management. You have led and developed engineers, made prioritization and performance decisions, hired thoughtfully, and delivered through a team—not only acted as its strongest individual contributor. Software-oriented production systems depth. You have built and operated distributed systems or reliability platforms and can reason across deployment behavior, Kubernetes, telemetry, service dependencies, and recovery mechanisms. Safe-change and performance judgment. You have led consequential migrations or incidents and used measurement to diagnose reliability or performance problems. You can distinguish symptoms from causes and validate fixes under realistic conditions. Platform-product and cross-team judgment. You can build capabilities other teams adopt, lead hands-on engagements without absorbing every service's operations, and make clear tradeoffs among reliability, performance, engineering effort, and cost. Nice to Have Experience with GitOps or progressive-delivery platforms such as Harness, ArgoCD, or Kargo. Experience with observability, profiling, load-testing, and failure-testing systems, including OpenTelemetry or comparable tooling. Experience with cloud cost attribution, capacity planning, and provider coordination, particularly on GCP. Experience growing distributed teams and using AI tools to increase engineering output while preserving production safeguards. Full-Time Employee Benefits Include: 💰 Competitive Salary & Equity 💹 401(k) Program with a 4% match ( US Only ) ⚕️ Health, Dental, Vision and Life Insurance 🩼 Short Term and Long Term Disability 🚼 Paid Parental, Medical, Caregiver Leave 🏝 Flexible Time Off (FTO) + Holidays 🚗 Commuter Benefits ( In-Office & US Only ) 📱 Monthly Wellness Stipend 🧑‍💻 Autonomous Work Environment 🖥 In Office Set-Up Reimbursement ( In-Office Only ) 🚀 Quarterly Team Gatherings ☕ In Office Amenities ( In-Office Only ) Want to learn more about what we are up to? Self-driving Company Replit Agent at Scale AI Adoption Build Open-Source Apps Interviewing + Culture at Replit Operating Principles Reasons not to work at Replit To achieve our mission of making programming more accessible around the world, we need our team to be representative of the world. descriptionAr: GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster. The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software. * Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license.
