An overview of this role As a Strategic Account Executive, you will own a portfolio of strategic and large customers and prospects in Poland, helping them get the most value from GitLab’s AI-powered DevSecOps platform. You’ll break into net new enterprise accounts and expand GitLab’s footprint within existing customers, using a consultative approach to understand their business needs and guide successful adoption and expansion of GitLab. You’ll work closely with pre- and post-sales teams and strategic channel partners to drive full-cycle sales, from prospecting and qualification through rollout, usage, and long-term growth, while acting as the voice of your customers by feeding their feedback and product ideas into GitLab’s public issue tracker. This role will need to be based remotely in UK, Ireland, Netherlands, France, Spain or Germany but selling to accounts in Poland. What you’ll do Own a portfolio of strategic and enterprise accounts, driving both net-new customer acquisition and expansion within existing customers. Lead complex sales cycles from prospecting and qualification through negotiation and close, using a consultative approach grounded in customer business needs. Develop and execute structured account plans that map customer priorities to GitLab’s DevSecOps and AI-powered platform capabilities. Collaborate closely with pre-sales, customer success, support, and strategic channel partners to ensure successful evaluations, rollouts, and long-term adoption of GitLab. Act as the voice of the customer by sharing feedback and product ideas through GitLab’s public issue tracker and with internal stakeholders. Generate and nurture qualified pipeline through targeted outreach, joint activities with channel partners, and effective use of existing relationships. Prepare and maintain accurate activity, pipeline, and forecast reports, and contribute to win/loss analysis to continuously improve sales execution. Partner with Marketing to shape and execute account-based and regional campaigns that support pipeline generation and expansion in your territory. What you’ll bring Experience owning and growing large, complex accounts, including both new business development and expansion within existing customers. Background selling into strategic or enterprise organizations, ideally within software, developer tools, or related technology environments. Ability to run a consultative sales process, from prospecting and discovery through proposal, negotiation, and closing. Demonstrated skill in account planning, forecast management, and coordinating cross-functional resources across pre-sales, post-sales, and support. Effective communicator who can translate customer needs into clear feedback for product, marketing, and technical teams. Comfortable discussing business value with senior stakeholders and aligning solutions to customer goals and challenges. Familiarity with Git, software development tools, or application lifecycle management, and ability to learn GitLab’s platform. Alignment with GitLab’s values and openness to bringing transferable experience from different industries or backgrounds. About the team You’ll join a regional Strategic Sales team that focuses on our largest and most complex customers in Central Europe. We own a defined list of strategic prospect and existing accounts and collaborate closely with Solutions Architects, Customer Success, Support, and Channel partners to drive both new customer acquisition and expansion of GitLab’s footprint. Our Strategic Sales team spend a lot of time collaborating and meeting with customers, so travel will be expected. We are focused on helping enterprise customers adopt the GitLab DevSecOps platform at scale, navigating complex buying centers, and shaping long-term partnerships that support customers’ business and technology goals.   How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being Flexible Paid Time Off  Team Member Resource Groups Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan Growth and Development Fund Parental Leave   Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. descriptionAr: About the Team OpenAI, in close collaboration with our capital partners, is building the world's most advanced AI infrastructure ecosystem. The Industrial Compute organization develops and delivers the large-scale power, data center, and compute infrastructure required to support frontier AI systems. The Data Center Engineering team works across energy, electrical, mechanical, controls, site development, construction, commissioning, operations, and external partners to turn demanding campus power requirements into safe, reliable, and executable solutions. About the Role We are seeking a Design Engineer, Power Generation to develop and integrate power-generation systems for large-scale AI infrastructure campuses. You will translate campus load, reliability, schedule, and operating requirements into practical generation architectures and technical design criteria, supporting both behind-the-meter generation and hybrid grid-and-generation strategies. This is an individual contributor role with broad technical ownership from early concept and technology evaluation through detailed design, equipment selection, construction support, commissioning, and performance validation. You will work with internal engineering teams, utilities, OEMs, EPC partners, developers, and operators to resolve interfaces, make disciplined tradeoffs, and establish repeatable power-generation designs that can scale across the portfolio. Key Responsibilities Develop power-generation concepts, reference architectures, design criteria, and site-specific requirements based on campus demand, phasing, reliability targets, grid availability, fuel strategy, site constraints, and operating objectives. Evaluate generation technologies and system configurations, including gas turbines, reciprocating engines, fuel cells, battery energy storage, microgrids, black-start systems, and hybrid grid-connected solutions. Define and review plant electrical and mechanical balance-of-plant requirements, protection and controls philosophy, grid-paralleling and islanding behavior, redundancy, maintainability, and operational modes. Translate AI infrastructure load profiles and deployment schedules into generation capacity plans, equipment sizing, ramp strategies, performance requirements, and commissioning criteria. Lead technical diligence of OEM, EPC, developer, and supplier proposals; review calculations, one-line diagrams, layouts, specifications, studies, schedules, and design assumptions to identify gaps and material risks. Coordinate interfaces across utility interconnection, substations, campus electrical distribution, cooling systems, controls, fuel supply, emissions, water, civil design, permitting, construction, and operations. Evaluate tradeoffs across availability, efficiency, emissions, cost, schedule, constructibility, scalability, maintainability, and long-term operating flexibility, and document clear technical recommendations. Support equipment selection, procurement, design reviews, factory and site acceptance testing, construction issue resolution, commissioning, performance testing, and operational handoff. Investigate design or field-performance issues, drive corrective actions with partners, and incorporate lessons learned into engineering standards, specifications, and future reference designs. Qualifications 8+ years of engineering experience in power generation or industrial power systems, including responsibility for generation facility design or integration. A bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. Experience taking generation projects from concept and equipment selection through detailed design, with direct involvement in procurement, construction support, commissioning, or performance testing. Strong understanding of generation technologies such as gas turbines or reciprocating engines and their supporting electrical, mechanical, and fuel systems, including protection, controls, grid paralleling, islanding, and black start. Ability to evaluate engineering studies, drawings, specifications, and supplier proposals; identify technical risks; and make defensible tradeoffs among safety, reliability, cost, schedule, and maintainability. Experience resolving design interfaces across engineering disciplines and coordinating equipment suppliers, engineering and construction partners, utilities, and operators. Sound judgment around safety, reliability, constructibility, maintainability, and technical risk, with the ability to make decisions when requirements or information are incomplete. Ability to document design requirements, assumptions, and decisions clearly and explain technical recommendations to engineering, delivery, commercial, and leadership teams. Preferred Skills Professional Engineer licensure and experience developing reusable engineering standards and reference designs across multiple projects. Hands-on experience deploying and commissioning onsite generation for campuses or industrial facilities with demand in the hundreds of megawatts or more, including large load steps and rapid power fluctuations. Experience co-designing and deploying battery energy storage systems (BESS) with onsite generation, including power and energy sizing, controls integration, load smoothing, and frequency support. Familiarity with utility interconnection studies, emissions and environmental constraints, fuel-supply requirements, and generation permitting. Experience validating generation and storage performance through dynamic studies and field testing, including load steps, load rejection, generator trips, and transitions between grid-connected and islanded operation. Experience delivering phased campus power, including integrating temporary generation, permanent generation, storage, and utility service while maintaining power to operating loads. descriptionAr: About Us At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company. At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in. Available Locations: London or Austin We are looking for a Product Manager to lead Safe Change for Cloudflare’s control plane. In this role, you will define how customers preview, stage, roll out, monitor, and recover from configuration changes. You will also shape platform foundations that enable internal teams to deploy changes with higher confidence, stronger guardrails, and lower operational risk. Cloudflare’s control plane converts dashboard and API changes into global network configurations. Today’s enterprise customers expect robust change-management features: deployment previews, gradual rollouts, quick rollbacks, versioning, traffic segmentation, data residency, auditability, and verification of applied state. You will own a high-leverage product domain spanning distributed systems, reliability, developer experience, and enterprise governance. Working closely with engineering and product leaders across the entire platform. You will help turn proven deployment safety patterns into reusable platform primitives across Cloudflare. This technical, highly collaborative role requires navigating architectural tradeoffs with engineers, evaluating risk and compliance with enterprise customers, and partnering with product and go-to-market teams to drive platform adoption. What you’ll do As a member of a growing team of infrastructure product managers your responsibilities include: Represent the customer, be it internal or external. Be the champion and voice of customers. Build intimate, personal customer relationships. Bring the customer's voice into the creation process. Develop the product vision for your area. Ensure that your vision can work not just for your current set of customers, but for 10 or even 100 times your current set.  Evangelize the vision so that all stakeholders are aligned, have context and understand where we are going. Make data-driven roadmap decisions.  Make tough tactical prioritization decisions based off of data you collect, curate, and disseminate.  Build trust with stakeholders by ensuring that your roadmap is understandable and sensible based on the data you present. Measure success. Own the measures used to define success for your product. Success measures must be defined at the inception of a product and tracked throughout its lifecycle. Make measures visible to all stakeholders and interpret them into actionable conclusions and new hypotheses. Author use cases and prioritize requirements. Translate observations and customer feedback into a prioritized product backlog.  Author use cases based on specific real-world product applications and extrapolate detailed product requirements for the scenarios. Collaborate across teams. We win or lose as a team. Product managers play a critical role in creating alignment between engineering teams and stakeholders. A collaborative attitude is essential to the job. Examples of desirable skills, knowledge, and experience The ideal candidate is customer-focused, data-driven, methodical and thrives in a goal-oriented and data-driven environment.  You have a deep technical understanding of the observability space and outstanding communication and collaboration skills.  You are able to work with a diverse group, get consensus, and drive the product forward.  You are execution focused, you emphasize getting things done while paying attention to important details. Maintain integrations between Knowledge Graph and the rest of the GitLab platform, working in areas that touch GitLab Rails, the Data Insights Platform (Siphon, NATS, ClickHouse), and GitLab Duo Agent Platform. Contribute to system design discussions by proposing options, raising questions, and documenting decisions, with a focus on reliability, scalability, and maintainability for analytical graph workloads. Improve the operational maturity of the service by adding or enhancing metrics, logging, runbooks, alerts, and small readiness tasks, and by participating in on-call rotation as appropriate for your level and experience. Collaborate asynchronously with product, data, infrastructure, security, and AI counterparts to clarify requirements, align on scope, and ship features safely for customers and sustainably for the team. You’ll build that record into GitLab’s source code experience, for humans and agents alike. Work through complex requirements and legacy constraints to deliver clear solutions while protecting the reliability of this critical system. Design and maintain backend services, APIs, data models, and business logic that support intuitive source code workflows. Collaborate across functions and teams, both asynchronously and synchronously, and involve domain experts when their input will improve the outcome. Use AI agents for well-scoped work when they can speed up delivery without sacrificing quality, and critically review their output. Write maintainable code that follows GitLab's standards and contribute to constructive code reviews. Help strengthen reliability by monitoring production health metrics, participating in Tier 2 on-call, troubleshooting incidents, contributing to root cause analysis, and improving observability and resiliency. Share knowledge through code review, technical documentation, and everyday collaboration while learning from others. What you’ll bring Professional experience building backend web applications, services, or application programming interfaces, with experience using Ruby and GraphQL. Experience with full-stack development to build and maintain user-facing workflows and their underlying systems. Experience writing backend unit and integration tests, with familiarity with the testing pyramid, Git, and collaborative code review processes. Clear written and spoken English communication skills, including sharing useful status updates in a remote, asynchronous environment. The ability to manage assigned priorities, work through ambiguity, take ownership of your work, and seek guidance when needed. Experience using AI coding agents to speed up software development while critically reviewing their output. Bonus: you’ve built agents or agent-based workflows that run in production, not just prototypes. About the team The functional team works across Europe and North America, supporting both synchronous and asynchronous collaboration. It includes four engineers, comprising both backend and frontend engineers. We work closely with other Source Code teams, Agentic Preview, Repository Services, and Hardening, as well as other teams in the company such as the Gitaly team, and the AI Governance team.   The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the EU, applicable in the specified country or countries only. Guide customers on how to best use the GitLab platform, including common DevSecOps best practices, Git workflows, CI/CD, and adoption patterns. Build and maintain Customer Success Plans, define critical goals and key performance indicators, and track progress with customers over time. Identify large-scale savings and reallocation opportunities and see them through to completion. Partner with People and R&D leaders on hiring plans, location strategy, and organizational design. Rethink planning, forecasting, and reporting workflows, and use AI tools to make them faster, more accurate, and more insightful. Redesign FP&A processes, policies, and planning and reporting systems for efficiency and effectiveness, with AI in the center. Work with Accounting on capitalized software, accruals, and allocations, and with Procurement on process improvements. Lead and develop your R&D finance team:: hire and coach team members, set goals and priorities, and give expert feedback. As Manager, Engineering, Git & Gitaly Operations, you'll lead the team responsible for the infrastructure layer underneath Git at GitLab: the open source Git project itself, Gitaly, GitLab's Git storage and remote procedure call layer, and the services that make Git perform at enterprise scale. Git and Gitaly are core to GitLab. If they go sideways in production, they affect everything downstream, including continuous integration, code review, and deployments. This role starts with genuine subject matter expertise in Git technologies and extends to reliable operation across GitLab's deployment models: Self-Managed, GitLab Dedicated, and SaaS. You'll build and develop a team with deep platform expertise and strong operational judgment. You'll partner across engineering groups to shape how Git and Gitaly operations evolve as the platform grows. What you’ll do Build and lead a team with deep platform expertise in Git and Gitaly, hiring and developing engineers who can operate this infrastructure layer with strong operational judgment. Own production reliability for Git and Gitaly across GitLab's full deployment footprint. Drive incident management, root cause investigation, and postmortems with the technical depth to distinguish a Git internals problem from a generic infrastructure problem. Design and operate Git and Gitaly service models that work across Self-Managed, GitLab Dedicated, and SaaS, with a clear view of which elements are common and which must differ between them. Maintain cloud-agnostic architecture and tooling decisions, avoiding designs that assume a single hyperscaler's primitives. Partner with the teams that own each deployment model so operational practices stay coherent rather than fragmenting into separate playbooks. Apply distributed systems fundamentals, including consistency, replication, and failure domains, to Gitaly's storage and replication model. Own elastic storage and compute strategy for Git repository data, including capacity planning, autoscaling, and consumption-based provisioning for GitLab's largest self-managed and SaaS customers. What you’ll bring Familiarity with GitLab's product and deployment models, and how Git and Gitaly support repository operations across self-managed, dedicated, and SaaS environments. Hands-on subject matter expertise in Git internals, including how the protocol, object model, and storage layer behave under load and at scale, not only familiarity with Git usage. Strong distributed systems fundamentals, including consistency, replication, failure handling, and horizontal scalability. Experience running production infrastructure across multiple deployment models, such as self-managed, dedicated or single-tenant, and multi-tenant SaaS, or a credible path from adjacent experience to it. Experience with elastic storage and compute, and consumption-based system design for variable, unpredictable load. People management experience, ideally leading site reliability engineering-style or platform operations teams. Direct experience with Gitaly, libgit2, JGit, or another Git implementation's internals is advantageous. Experience operating cloud-agnostic infrastructure across multiple hyperscalers or on-premises environments is advantageous. About the team The Git & Gitaly Operations team owns the Git infrastructure layer that powers GitLab and works at the intersection of Git internals, distributed systems, storage, and production operations. We expect the Git & Gitaly Operations team to go deep on one of GitLab's most critical platforms. The work requires technical depth, strong operational discipline, and the ability to solve complex reliability and scaling challenges in Git and Gitaly. An overview of this role As a Fullstack Engineer on the Duo Client SDK team at GitLab, you'll build the shared foundation for every GitLab Duo client. Today, the logic that powers Duo in editors lives inside the GitLab Language Server. We're extracting it into a true software development kit (SDK): a set of well-versioned TypeScript packages that editor extensions, our web-based Duo Chat on GitLab.com, and eventually external applications can use. You'll work in TypeScript across frontend and backend systems. You'll design the SDK's Node.js core and public application programming interface (API), and work in the clients that use it. The work rewards care about interfaces, versioning, and backward compatibility as much as features because other engineers will depend on what you build. You'll have senior and staff engineers alongside you to help with design. You'll own the implementation of scoped packages and ship improvements with minimal guidance while collaborating with the team on larger architectural changes. Some examples of our projects: The Duo Client SDK, extracting versioned, publishable packages from the GitLab Language Server The GitLab Language Server, rebuilt on top of the SDK as our polyglot surface Duo Chat on the web, as one of the SDK's first consumers What you'll do Develop secure, well-tested, and performant TypeScript features that solve technical problems of moderate scope and complexity. Ship small features and improvements with minimal guidance, writing tests with every merge request and contributing to code reviews and design discussions. Extract and publish TypeScript packages from the GitLab Language Server, migrating consumers incrementally so no parallel implementation is left to drift. Design durable public APIs with clear interfaces, semantic versioning, changelogs, and deprecation paths for external consumers. Build isomorphic core packages that isolate platform-specific behavior in adapters at the edges. Build and improve SDK client surfaces, including Vue 3 components in Duo Chat on the web, in collaboration with product, design, and engineering teams. Strengthen credential handling across hosts, including bearer tokens, session cookies, and CSRF protection. Optimize bundle size, startup cost, and dependency weight for browser consumers, and support a Tier 2 on-call rotation for urgent engineering issues. What you'll bring Strong proficiency with TypeScript across frontend and backend systems, including experience building and maintaining Node.js services. Experience with modern build and packaging tools, including monorepos, multi-module builds, ECMAScript modules (ESM), and dependency management. Experience with Vue 3 and the Composition API, or comparable component-based frontend experience and a willingness to learn Vue. Experience designing APIs that other people use, with the ability to explain what you'd do differently. Understanding of the differences between running code in Node.js and in the browser, and how to write code that works in both. A security-minded development approach, including careful credential handling and performance optimization. Ability to communicate clearly and concisely in writing about technical problems, propose iterative solutions, and work effectively in an agile environment. Self-motivation, strong organizational skills, and the judgment to ask for help when needed while thriving in a fully remote organization aligned with GitLab's values. Strong attention to detail and the ability to organize and prioritize multiple reports or work items. Experience with a bug bounty or vulnerability disclosure platform such as HackerOne or Bugcrowd. descriptionAr: About Us At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company. At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in. Location: Austin (Hybrid) About the team The Data Intelligence & Analytics organization builds the core data platform and internal products that power decision-making across the company. We design and operate large-scale data systems, own the company’s data lake, ingestion infrastructure, and platform tooling, and develop end-to-end applications that transform complex datasets into fast, reliable, business-critical products used daily by go-to-market, product, and engineering teams. Our work sits at the intersection of data platforms, distributed systems, and product development, giving engineers the opportunity to own meaningful problems across the stack, build specialized data solutions for predictive modeling and machine learning applications, and construct systems that truly run the business. About the role We are looking for an experienced Data Engineer to join our Austin team and help scale the development of our internal data products. In this role, you will build data-driven applications that empower teams across the company, including go-to-market, engineering, and product. Because the products we build are initiated and owned by the team, you will be involved end-to-end — from shaping requirements and designing features to implementation and long-term ownership. You will work on building scalable, reliable systems that solve critical business problems, partnering closely with full-stack engineers to develop new features and operate the data pipelines and services behind our applications. Our stack spans multiple languages and technologies, including Go, Scala, and ClickHouse, and continues to evolve. Many of our products also incorporate strong AI components, giving you opportunities to build sophisticated, AI-ready data layers and work with modern AI infrastructure and tools such as vector databases, MCP-based services, and Workers AI. What you'll do Design and implement core components of our data pipelines and services in Go and Scala, with a focus on scalability, performance, and long-term maintainability. Partner closely with engineers, analysts, and product stakeholders to design solutions for strategic initiatives, business-critical data products, and agentic AI architectures. Contribute to the evolution of our data platform architecture, improving scalability, reliability, observability, and data correctness across the stack. Build and curate high-quality, well-modeled, and richly contextual datasets that power internal products, predictive analytics, and LLM-enabled features at company scale. Develop a deep understanding of the company’s data ecosystem — including source systems, tooling, and data flows — and collaborate closely with the data and system engineers in Austin, Lisbon, and London to improve data ingestion, quality, and governance. Lead by example through design reviews, knowledge sharing, and mentorship, helping raise the technical bar, data engineering practices, and AI implementation standards across the organization. Examples of desirable skills, knowledge and experience B.S. or M.S. in Computer Science, Engineering, Statistics, Mathematics, or a related quantitative field, or equivalent practical experience. 5+ years of professional experience in data engineering, software engineering, or related roles, building and operating production data systems. Strong programming expertise in Go, Python, or JVM-based languages, with experience writing high-quality, production-grade services and pipelines. Deep knowledge of SQL and hands-on experience designing data models and working with relational, analytical, or vector databases (e.g., PostgreSQL, MySQL, ClickHouse). Experience building scalable, reliable, and observable data pipelines, with an understanding of performance, data quality, and operational best practices. Proven problem-solving and communication skills, with a track record of driving projects in ambiguous environments and partnering effectively with cross-functional teams. Familiarity with Google Cloud Platform, foundational Large Language Model (LLM) orchestration frameworks, or something similar. descriptionAr: About the team OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood, as it leaves the lab and meets the world. This company works at the frontier of intelligence. Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told, in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning. About the role We’re looking for a Designer to create thoughtful, high-quality work across consumer campaigns and brand identity. You’ll contribute original ideas and turn creative direction into finished design across campaigns, digital experiences, social content, presentations, and brand materials. This is a hands-on maker role for someone who enjoys moving between concept development and detailed execution. You’ll work closely with creative leads, writers, marketers, and producers, bringing strong visual craft and an active interest in using AI tools to explore and develop creative work. In this role, you will: Develop visual ideas for consumer campaigns and brand initiatives, exploring multiple directions and explaining how each supports the brief. Translate creative direction into polished designs across digital, social, presentation, and campaign formats, with careful attention to typography and composition. Contribute to identity and campaign systems, carrying a clear visual idea through layouts, imagery, and related assets. Partner with writers, art directors, motion designers, and producers to connect words and visuals and prepare work for production. Use AI-enabled tools to explore concepts and generate variations, applying design judgment to select, refine, and integrate useful results. Build and maintain reusable templates and assets within established brand systems, keeping files organized and handoffs clear. Incorporate feedback, check finished work across formats, and communicate progress and constraints so collaborators can plan around delivery. You might thrive in this role if you have: A portfolio showing strong visual ideas and execution across brand identity, campaigns, or related graphic design work. A solid command of typography, layout, composition, image-making, and visual hierarchy, with close attention to production detail. The ability to contribute to concept development and independently execute defined deliverables in collaboration with a creative lead. Proficiency in Figma, Adobe Creative Suite, or equivalent tools, with experience preparing files for collaborative design and production workflows. Practical curiosity about AI-assisted creative workflows and the ability to assess generated work critically rather than accept it as finished design. Clear communication, openness to critique, and the ability to manage multiple assignments as priorities and creative directions evolve. Experience with consumer or technology brands, motion, illustration, or creative coding is helpful. We value a portfolio that makes your own contribution and design process clear. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. You'll have meaningful budget, strong creative and technical partners, and the autonomy to build a program that creates qualified pipeline and strengthens our brand. This is a hands-on role. We want someone who knows their channels inside out, enjoys getting into the details, and can take a campaign from initial hypothesis through execution, analysis, and optimization. You'll have access to specialist support when it makes sense, but you'll be the person driving the work. We also believe AI creates an opportunity for exceptional individual contributors to do work that previously required much larger teams. We're looking for someone who is already exploring that opportunity and wants to push it further. What makes this role interesting You get to build with the resources most marketers wish they had. Paid is relatively underdeveloped at Ashby compared with the scale of our business. You get to build something substantial without unwinding years of accumulated complexity or fighting for the resources to make it work. We have strong content, customer proof, product differentiation, and an established brand. You'll start with a monthly budget in the hundreds of thousands of dollars and the support of our design, web, and RevOps teams. You can rethink how paid marketing gets done. We want to enable exceptional individual contributors to accomplish more through AI, automation, and better workflows. You'll have the freedom to experiment with new tools, build systems that improve your output, and challenge established ways of working. You'll build a program that makes the brand and business stronger. We believe great paid marketing combines analytical rigor with creative judgment. You'll optimize for pipeline and efficiency while building campaigns that earn attention, communicate our differentiation, and give the right buyers a reason to care about Ashby. We don't want a lead-generation machine that makes our brand worse. What you'll own Build and scale our paid program. Own strategy and execution across LinkedIn, Meta, and Google Search, expanding into YouTube and other channels as opportunities emerge. Prioritize audiences, develop campaign hypotheses, manage budgets, and turn promising experiments into repeatable sources of qualified pipeline. Drive creative strategy and experimentation. Develop campaign concepts, write ad copy, brief creative, and shape landing-page tests. Work closely with design, content, and product marketing to produce distinctive work. Build a disciplined testing cadence across audiences, creative, offers, and conversion paths, knowing when to scale, iterate, or stop. Use AI to increase your impact. Build practical workflows using AI, agents, and automation to improve research, creative iteration, campaign operations, and analysis. We want someone who actively experiments with new approaches, evaluates their effectiveness, and turns what works into repeatable systems. Own measurement and performance. Drive our approach to paid measurement in partnership with RevOps. Establish the signals and reporting needed to understand qualified reach, conversion, pipeline contribution, and efficiency. Develop better ways to assess incrementality, make informed decisions with imperfect attribution, and translate performance data into clear investment recommendations. Connect campaigns to the buyer journey. Partner with sales, lifecycle, and ABM to understand what makes an opportunity valuable and how paid can influence the journey from first touch through pipeline. Adapt messaging and investment to our customer segments and markets. What you'll work on in your first six months Take ownership of LinkedIn, identifying opportunities to improve qualified reach, creative, and progression into pipeline. Build and scale Meta, establishing a strong creative testing cadence and the landing pages and follow-up needed to make the channel work. Expand Google Search and launch YouTube, evaluating additional channels where there's a compelling audience and learning opportunity. Establish a stronger operating system for paid, including AI-enabled workflows, measurement, and a clear approach to allocating investment. The goal isn't to scale every channel equally. It's to build a broad set of opportunities, learn quickly, and concentrate investment where the evidence is strongest. You've personally built and scaled programs in sales-led B2B SaaS. You're a builder, not just a strategist. You're excited to get into the accounts, develop the creative, run experiments, investigate performance, and solve problems yourself. You know when external expertise can help, but you don't need an agency to do the core work. You combine analytical rigor with creative taste. You understand performance metrics and experimentation, but you also know what makes advertising compelling. You can connect campaign decisions to buyer quality and pipeline without losing sight of the brand you're building. You're already changing how you work with AI. You can demonstrate how you've used AI too

descriptionAr: About PostHog PostHog is your product’s context layer. It ingests and stores your analytics, errors, replays, and business data so you and your agents can query and act on it. We launched out of Y Combinator's W20 cohort . We've since shipped more than a dozen products, including: A suite of analytics and observability tools, including product analytics , replay vision , AI observability , and error tracking PostHog MCP for users and their agents to query and act on their product and business data Data warehouse so users can query product and customer data together using custom SQL insights. We are: Product-led . More than 500K organizations have installed PostHog, mostly driven by word-of-mouth. We have intensely strong product-market fit. Default alive . Revenue is growing incredibly quickly, and we're very efficient. We raise money to push ambition and grow faster, not to keep the lights on. Well-funded. We've raised more than $180m from some of the world's top investors. We're set up for a long, ambitious journey. We're focused on building an awesome product for end users, hiring exceptional teammates, shipping fast, and being as weird as possible . Things we care about Transparency: Everyone can read about our roadmap, how we pay (or even let go of) people, our strategy, and how we work, in our public company handbook . Internally, we share revenue, notes and slides from board meetings, and fundraising plans, so everyone has the context they need to make good decisions. Autonomy: We don’t tell anyone what to do. Everyone chooses what to work on next based on what's going to have the biggest impact on our customers, and what they find interesting and motivating to work on. Engineers lead product teams and make product decisions . Teams are flexible and easy to change when needed. Shipping fast: Why not now? We want to build a lot of products; we can't do that shipping at a normal pace. We've built the company around small teams – autonomous, highly-efficient groups of cracked engineers who can outship much larger companies because they own their products end-to-end. Time for building: Nothing gets shipped in a meeting. We're a natively remote company. We default to async communication – PRs > Issues > Slack. Tuesdays and Thursdays are meeting-free days , and we prioritize heads down building time over perfect coordination. This will be the most productive job you've ever had. Being weird: Weird means redesigning an already world-class website for the 5th time. It means shipping literally every product that relates to customer data. It means building an objectively unnecessary developer toy with dubious shareholder value. Doing weird stuff is a competitive advantage. And it's fun. Who we’re looking for We're looking for a Technical Support Engineer who loves helping customers and can't leave a problem alone until it's solved. You're an engineer who happens to do support. You pick up new things fast and you're comfortable with a problem nobody has seen before. That matters more to us than your previous job title, and people on our team came to support from various backgrounds. You care about how a customer feels when they leave the conversation, not only whether the ticket closed. You take feedback well, say when you don't know something yet, and learn from anyone on the team. What you’ll be doing Helping customers across all of PostHog's products, in the app and in shared Slack channels with our bigger customers Owning your tickets from beginning to end, and keeping customers updated along the way Shipping fixes to the PostHog codebase and docs when you find something broken or unclear Becoming the support expert for a product area: owning its queue, working closely with the engineering team behind it, and spotting the patterns that turn into fixes Improving how we do support, including the tooling and workflows we build on PostHog itself Passing customer pain points and feature requests to engineering teams with enough context for them to prioritize What you won’t be doing ❌ You won't be routing tickets, or forwarding hard questions to engineering because they look hard. ❌ You won't say "that's not my job". If you can't solve something, you find who can and make the connection. ❌ You also won't be pasting AI answers back to customers. We use AI every day, but we expect you to test things out for yourself and write a reply to the customer that's better than the one it would write. Here's more on how we think about that . How we work You'll be the face of PostHog for many of our customers. Most of them are engineers, so they want help from someone who understands the technical detail and writes back like a person. We want support to be part of why people choose PostHog. We provide support across EU and US time zones, and we're hiring in both. We work in public by default, so you'll ask for help, share what you learn, and discuss problems in team channels rather than DMs. Read more about how the support team works and our company values . Requirements Experience in at least two programming languages, whether from a previous role, side projects, or something else Experience debugging unfamiliar code or systems, and checking your fix works Clear, concise writing that explains a complex fix without burying the customer in options Thorough investigations that don't slow down your reply to the customer Good at prioritizing and context switching across a busy queue that spans many products Nice to have Experience supporting similar products, e.g. analytics, session replay, feature flags, experiments, or LLM observability A background in support, teaching, product, or another role where you explain technical things to people If you have a disability, please let us know if there's any way we can make the interview process better for you - we're happy to accommodate! #LI-DNI

Available Location: Los Angeles, CA What you will do as a Customer Engineer The Customer Engineer (CE) is the core driver of our technical go-to-market strategy: a trusted technical advisor and primary architect of the customer journey. You will bridge the gap between technical strategy and business value—guiding enterprise clients from initial pre-sales technical validation through onboarding, deployment architecture, and full lifecycle expansion. Sitting within the GTM organization and reporting to a Customer Engineering Leader, you will not hand off your customers once an initial agreement is reached. Deliver tailored technical presentations, architectural diagrams, and demonstrations that show how Cloudflare solves specific performance, security, and reliability challenges. Proactively address complex technical objections, security compliance questions, and edge-case architectural requirements during the sales cycle. Take accountability for a suitable solution deployment strategy (Customer, Partner or Cloudflare Professional services) being an integral part of all proposals. Customer Adoption & Value Realization: Provide oversight to technical onboarding and implementation, but not execute the implementation, serving as the primary executive and engineering contact for the customer. Design structured migration and onboarding blueprints tailored to the customer’s environment (e.g. DNS migrations, Zero Trust rollouts, WAF tuning guidance), and act as the lead consultant for customer engineering teams, walking them step-by-step through configuration best practices.  Partner with Account Executives to own discovery, demos, onboarding, technical health, risk, and expansion strategy. Proactively monitor customer health scores and telemetry to ensure rapid time-to-value, resolve integration bottlenecks, and reduce deployment risk. Commercial Accountability & Expansion: Carry a variable quota tied directly to new business acquisition and/or ongoing account growth. Be commercially accountable for ensuring deep platform adoption, retaining revenue, and identifying strategic cross-sell and up-sell opportunities based on product usage data. Lead technical Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) to translate platform capabilities into return on investment for C-level executives. Trusted Advisory: Act as a trusted technical advisor throughout the entire customer lifecycle, maintaining a continuous, deep relationship with key stakeholders from initial onboarding through maturity, renewal, and expansion. Provide thought partnership on architecture, AI control layers, security posture, and deployment confidence. Identify potential deployment risks or integration bottlenecks early, and provide remediation strategies to de-risk customer outcomes.  AI Orchestration & Workflow Automation: Leverage AI agents, Large Language Models (LLMs), and internal platforms to automate routine tasks such as RFP/Security Questionnaire responses, sandbox provisioning, basic telemetry monitoring, and internal/external documentation, reclaiming your time for strategic customer advisory. Education & Enablement: Partner closely with the Enablement Team to design, build, and govern technical resources. Available Locations: Austin, TX | New York, NY | San Francisco, CA | Seattle, WA | London, UK or Germany About the Role Cloudflare's Developer Platform powers stateful, data-intensive applications across our network. We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer to work across the database stack, from query planning and execution to transaction processing and durable storage. You'll make decisions that shape the consistency, durability, and latency guarantees that customer applications rely on. Correctness under concurrency and failure is central to the role. You'll define and implement how queries read and modify data, how concurrent transactions become visible, and how durable state is recovered. You'll validate these systems using deterministic simulation, workload testing, and evidence from production. Responsibilities Improve query planning and execution, including index selection, row reads and writes, and performance as data volumes and access patterns change. Build transaction and storage paths that make writes durable and reads consistent. Define when changes become visible, how commits survive failure, and how recovery restores a correct view of the data. Design deterministic simulations that make rare event orderings and failures reproducible. Plan stateful upgrades that cannot be reversed by rolling back software. Carry them through staged rollout, failover, and recovery without putting existing data at risk. Participate in the service's on-call rotation and incident response. Own major changes from design through production. Coordinate implementation across teams when a change spans multiple parts of the service, and help trace failures across those parts. Mentor other engineers through design reviews, debugging, and incident analysis involving concurrency, durability, and recovery. Desirable Skills, Knowledge & Experience You have owned a database, storage engine, transaction system, or similarly correctness-sensitive stateful system from architecture through production. You can make architecture and implementation decisions when requirements or system boundaries are incomplete. You understand how query execution, indexing, transaction processing, and durable state shape what developers and operators observe. You understand how concurrency control, isolation, replication, and snapshots shape consistency, durability, and recovery. You can apply those concepts when operations arrive out of order, components fail independently, or the network partitions. You write and debug concurrent production software in Rust, Go, C++, or another systems language. You can trace failures across process, network, and durable-state boundaries. You have operated stateful systems through rollouts, scaling events, incidents, and recovery. You know the difference between transient unavailability and incomplete or incorrect recovery, and when a system is safe to return to service. You have led investigations where failures crossed systems owned by several teams. Bonus Points You've worked on the internals of PostgreSQL, MySQL, Amazon Aurora, or another relational database and can trace a SQL operation from planning through commit. Your work on transaction processing or concurrency control has included defining snapshot visibility and recovery behavior. You've profiled database workloads and traced performance bottlenecks from query execution through durable storage. You've used deterministic simulation or another systematic method to uncover distributed-systems bugs that conventional tests missed. descriptionAr: SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars. SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next. About the Role As a Solutions Architect, you’ll work with some of the world’s most sophisticated organizations to answer a new question: what should a company look like when AI agents become part of how work gets done? We’re hiring Solutions Architects to help strategic customers make AI-native work real in production on the Grok platform, using Grok Bot for knowledge work and business workflows and Grok Build (Cursor) for AI-native software development. This is a hands-on technical role within the Customer Success organization, where you’ll partner with AI Deployment Managers (ADMs) to own the technical track across architecture, workflow redesign, and enterprise security while helping organizations rethink how they operate and how they build software with AI. You’ll help customers move from excitement to workflows teams rely on every day by discovering real job friction, integrating Grok Build into codebases, CI pipelines, and code review, and designing scoped Grok Bot workflows with human-in-the-loop judgment. The best Solutions Architects pair technical credibility with product instincts and extreme ownership, and they are as comfortable debugging a CI workflow or leading an architecture review as helping executives, from CTOs to the CRO, CMO, CFO, and COO, understand where AI changes how the business runs and how software is built. What You’ll Do Help Engineering Teams Adopt AI-Native Development with Grok Build (Cursor) Roll out Grok Build across strategic engineering organizations and integrate it into real codebases and production workflows rather than isolated demos. Configure developer environments, repository rules, and conventions, and run hands-on enablement that drives fast, durable adoption. Bring agentic SDLC practices into the customer’s delivery process, from planning and implementation through testing, CI, and code review, and clear developer workflow friction along the way. Keep a strong hands-on Build baseline by shipping runnable, convention-driven work in Grok Build yourself. Engage Customers on the Grok Bot Journey Use Grok Bot to turn a business user’s problem into an accepted user story and requirements that flow into Jira and through the agentic SDLC in Grok Build. descriptionAr: Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X . We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do. You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity. About Grafana Labs:  There are more than 700,000 active installations of Grafana around the globe, monitoring everything from beehives to climate change in the Alps. The instantly recognizable dashboards have been spotted everywhere from a SpaceX launch and Minecraft HQ to Wimbledon and the Tour de France. Grafana Labs also helps companies including Bloomberg, JPMorgan Chase, and eBay manage their observability strategies with full-stack offerings that can be run fully managed with Grafana Cloud, or self-managed with Grafana Enterprise Stack. The Grafana stack has grown to include more open-source projects, including Grafana Loki (for logs) and Grafana Tempo (for traces) and Grafana Mimir (for metrics). Description of Duties We’re looking for a Staff Technical Writer to create documentation and learning content that helps people adopt and master Grafana’s observability products. You’ll work with engineers, product managers, and the Grafana writing team to produce content for a range of products and audiences, from first-time users to experienced practitioners. Because our products and priorities evolve, we’re looking for someone who learns new technical domains quickly. AI is part of how this team works. We use AI-assisted workflows and tools throughout the content lifecycle, from research and drafting to review, validation, and maintenance. You’ll use these tools every day and help the team get better at using them. Key Responsibilities Plan, research, write, and maintain documentation and learning content (concepts, tasks, tutorials, references, and in-product learning) that supports adoption and long-term product mastery. Use AI tools and workflows to work faster and at a higher quality: drafting, structuring, technical validation, consistency checks, and keeping content current. You apply human judgment to everything AI produces and take responsibility for its accuracy. Contribute to the team’s shared AI workflows and skills, and look for ways to improve and automate how we create and maintain content as tools and models evolve. Partner with engineers, PMs, and other stakeholders to understand product requirements, interview subject matter experts, and turn complex technical detail into clear, accurate content. Test what you document. Run the software, follow your own procedures, and flag product and UX gaps you find along the way. Let data guide your priorities. We have strong docs and learning analytics. You’ll use them, along with user feedback, to find content gaps, prioritize your work, and show the impact of what you ship. Work with the documentation manager and other writers to improve information architecture, voice, and consistency across our docs, and to make information easy to find for both people and AI-driven search and assistants. Manage several projects at once, using judgment to prioritize and communicate clearly when the plan changes. Mentor teammates and share practices that raise the quality of the team’s work. Requirements What experience would make someone be successful in this role? Experience writing or documenting enterprise or developer-facing software, with a portfolio or writing samples that show technical depth. Hands-on experience using AI tools and models in your writing workflow (such as LLM assistants, agentic coding tools, or custom prompts and skills), and the ability to explain how you evaluate and verify their output. Experience working with docs-as-code: command-line Git, GitHub (pull requests and reviews), Markdown, and common IDEs. Comfort working in technical environments. You can set up, run, and troubleshoot software yourself to verify what you write (for example, command line, containers, or Kubernetes, or a willingness to learn quickly). Experience collaborating with engineers and product managers to get accurate technical information. Experience working remotely and asynchronously on a distributed team. What you’ll bring to the role Curiosity about AI as a craft. You treat AI workflows as a professional skill. You experiment, share what works, and know where AI helps and where it doesn’t. Technical credibility. You care about accuracy, you learn new technical domains quickly, and you ask questions until you understand them. Strong judgment and editing skills. You can tell good content from plausible-sounding content, and you hold the line on quality. Ownership. You manage multiple projects and work well both independently and collaboratively. Clarity. You write concisely and plainly for readers of all experience levels. Bonus: Experience with observability, monitoring, or cloud-native tooling, or con

descriptionAr: About Us At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company. At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in. Available Locations: Singapore or Sydney About the department In this role, you will be focused on maintaining the Cloudflare global network. You'll work closely with Cloudflare’s SRE (Site Reliability Engineering) team, Network Engineering team, Network Deployment Engineering team and with various vendors and partners (including hardware vendors, datacenter and network providers, and ISPs) to maintain and improve our global infrastructure. You will further be responsible for the development and implementation of consistent processes and visibility measurements for consistent and effective management of our infrastructure. This is a highly visible position that requires deep technical understanding of datacenter infrastructure, networking (physical), and basic experience with data analysis and project management. To be successful in this position, you should have excellent technical skills, communication skills, and be able to navigate a range of challenges and constraints (e.g. schedule adherence, time zones, and cultures). You will have the opportunity to (literally) build a faster, safer Internet for our millions of users and the billions of web surfers that visit their sites each month. Who you are You will thrive in a hypergrowth engineering environment and be self driven with a keen attention to detail. You will come with a deep technical understanding of Data Center colocation environments, network architecture and server technologies. You will be used to working through partners to support infrastructure delivery to a number of remote locations. You will have had experience managing operational environments, and used to developing new approaches to improve delivery efficiency or operational stability.  What you'll do Collaborating with internal teams (Infrastructure, Network Engineering and SRE). Create documentation and manage remote contractors to complete datacenter tasks, working with hardware manufacturers, datacenter and network providers, logistics partners and other service providers in support of our 330+ cities and 125+ countries Maintain Data Center environment operational availability Leverage AI tools to automate repetitive operational tasks, accelerate documentation, and speed up troubleshooting and root-cause analysis Creating and maintaining documentation, plans, SOP’s, MOP’s etc. Support and configure network infrastructure where required Providing feedback to internal teams to support internal tools and external vendor partnerships Required Experience Experience with Juniper, Cisco and DWDM network equipment Minimum of 4 years experience of Linux systems administration Experience managing and instructing remote contractors  Familiarity with work required to stand up infrastructure in remote colocation facilities  Experience running and improving operational processes, including automation tooling, in a rapidly changing environment Familiarity with day-to-day tasks and projects common to Data Center Operations (deployment, migration, decommissioning etc.) Comfortable handling basic program management responsibilities (prioritization, planning, scheduling, status reporting) such as JIRA Participate in a shared on-call rotation to maintain 24×7 operational availability of the global network. descriptionAr: About the Team OpenAI's data center construction teams work with engineering, supply chain, safety, quality, commissioning and operations partners to deliver the infrastructure that supports our computing needs. Mechanical delivery brings together cooling equipment, plant, piping and controls interfaces so that systems are installed, tested and ready for commissioning. About the Role As a Mechanical Lead, you will lead mechanical field delivery for data center construction, including cooling infrastructure, mechanical yards, piping and data hall fit-out. You will oversee general contractors, specialist installers and service providers, combining practical mechanical expertise with hands-on field leadership. Your focus will be safe installation, contractor performance, coordinated interfaces and complete evidence for commissioning and operational handover. Key Responsibilities Manage mechanical contractors, equipment and piping installers, and general-contractor interfaces against approved scope, schedule and quality requirements. Oversee installation readiness and delivery of cooling plant, pumps, heat rejection equipment, air handling, piping and applicable liquid-cooling infrastructure. Coordinate equipment placement, pipe routing, supports, access and maintainability with structural, electrical, controls and hardware teams. Review contractor work plans, constructability, submittals, RFIs and change proposals; resolve field issues with the responsible engineering teams. Oversee pressure testing, flushing, cleaning and inspection records; verify completion, defect closure and commissioning readiness. Support commissioning specialists with mechanical startup and system tests, corrective work and complete as-built, operating and maintenance documentation. Set contractor priorities, review staffing and progress, identify constraints early and coordinate recovery actions with construction leadership. Maintain clear progress, risk and change reporting, with accountable handoffs between construction partners and OpenAI teams. Qualifications Substantial mechanical construction, installation, field engineering or startup experience in data center cooling or comparable critical facilities. Demonstrated leadership of mechanical contractors or crews, including coordination across organizations without relying on direct reporting authority. Practical knowledge of cooling, ventilation, hydronic and pumping systems, heat rejection, piping cleanliness and vendor startup requirements. Ability to review drawings, specifications, submittals, work methods and controls narratives for constructability and installation readiness. Experience coordinating inspection, pressure testing, flushing, cleaning, balancing prerequisites and controls checkout. Ability to interpret test results and deficiency records with commissioning specialists and coordinate corrective work, retesting and turnover evidence. Clear communication and sound judgment when coordinating power, controls, startup and testing dependencies or escalating safety and delivery risks. Relevant trade, apprenticeship, technical or degree-based preparation, or equivalent practical experience. Preferred Skills Owner-side or specialist-contractor experience with high-density data center cooling, liquid cooling or phased cooling-system startup. Experience with integrated systems testing, factory or site acceptance activities, and digital commissioning or field-reporting tools. Relevant mechanical trade, controls, balancing or commissioning qualifications, or professional engineering credentials. descriptionAr: About the Team OpenAI's Industrial Compute organization delivers the infrastructure that powers frontier AI models. Within Infrastructure Delivery, we turn engineering concepts into safe, reliable, and operational AI campuses by working across design, construction, utilities, commissioning, operations, and external partners. The fire protection function establishes the life-safety and property-protection strategy for these campuses. The team connects code requirements and engineering standards to practical design, construction, testing, incident readiness, and long-term operations. About the Role We are seeking a Fire Protection Engineer to lead owner-side fire and life-safety engineering across large-scale data center programs. You will establish design criteria, review complex fire protection systems, coordinate with authorities and delivery partners, and ensure that fire and life-safety requirements remain clear from early design through construction, commissioning, and operational handover. This role requires strong technical judgment across detection, alarm, suppression, smoke control, water supply, emergency response, and code compliance. You will work closely with engineering, construction, safety, security, commissioning, and operations teams to resolve risks quickly without compromising life safety, reliability, or schedule. Key Responsibilities Develop and maintain fire protection and life-safety design criteria, technical standards, and review requirements for self-build data center campuses. Review fire protection drawings, specifications, code analyses, fire and life-safety narratives, hydraulic calculations, equipment submittals, and sequences of operation across all project phases. Provide owner-side engineering direction for fire detection and alarm, automatic suppression, fire pumps and water storage, smoke control, emergency communication, and related life-safety systems. Integrate fire protection requirements with architectural, structural, electrical, mechanical, controls, security, hardware, and operational systems. Partner with code officials, authorities having jurisdiction, insurers, consultants, contractors, and equipment vendors to resolve code interpretations and approval risks. Support constructability reviews, RFIs, submittals, field inspections, deficiency resolution, and change management during active construction. Define commissioning, integrated-system testing, acceptance, turnover, and operational-readiness criteria for fire and life-safety systems. Assess fire and life-safety risks associated with high-density compute, battery and energy-storage systems, generators and fuel systems, utility infrastructure, cooling systems, hazardous materials, and construction activities. Support incident response, root-cause reviews, corrective actions, and lessons learned, translating operational findings into improved designs and standards. Maintain clear records of design decisions, code positions, approvals, testing results, open risks, and turnover requirements. Travel regularly to project sites to support design reviews, field execution, testing, commissioning, and operational readiness. Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Fire Protection Engineering or a related engineering discipline, or equivalent practical experience delivering fire and life-safety systems. 8+ years of fire protection engineering experience supporting data centers, industrial facilities, advanced manufacturing, energy infrastructure, or other mission-critical environments. Strong knowledge of applicable building and fire codes and standards, including IBC, IFC, NFPA requirements, and local authority approval processes. Technical depth in fire alarm and detection, water-based suppression, special-hazard suppression, fire pumps and water supply, smoke control, egress, and integrated life-safety systems. Experience reviewing fire protection designs, specifications, hydraulic calculations, equipment submittals, testing procedures, and commissioning results. Demonstrated ability to work with authorities having jurisdiction, engineering consultants, contractors, insurers, vendors, and internal stakeholders. Experience resolving field issues and design changes while maintaining clear code compliance, safety, quality, schedule, and documentation. Strong written and verbal communication, sound engineering judgment, and the ability to create clarity when requirements or ownership are ambiguous. Professional Engineer licensure in Fire Protection Engineering, or the ability to obtain licensure in relevant jurisdictions. Preferred Skills Experience with hyperscale data centers, high-density compute environments, or global multi-site infrastructure programs. Experience with battery rooms, energy-storage systems, generator plants, fuel systems, high-voltage substations, or other campus utility infrastructure. Familiarity with performance-based design, fire and smoke modeling, quantitative risk assessment, or fire-hazard analysis. Experience leading integrated testing and coordinating fire alarm, suppression, controls, security, mechanical, and electrical interfaces. Experience developing reusable standards, design templates, commissioning requirements, and incident-prevention programs across multiple sites.
