In an acceleratingly dangerous world, the scope of that mission has changed. We are becoming something more: critical infrastructure. Banks run their payment rails on us. Governments run public services on us. Media companies depend on us during live events. Health systems depend on us to provide care. Reliability for these customers is no longer a feature of our product. It is a mission. Serving that customer base demands a different operating model. Traditional support organizations route tickets. Traditional engineering organizations ship features. Neither alone is enough when the stakes are this high. We are pivoting to something different: a customer-facing engineering organization, directly engaged with our customers at scale. This is work a central dev team cannot do from the inside of the network. The Customer Reliability Engineering function is the spine of that pivot. CRE is SRE applied outward, the same engineering discipline, applied to the reliability of the systems our customers run on Cloudflare. You are the engineer who owns the problems that matter most to the customers who matter most, and you contribute directly to our products and tooling, in partnership with Product Engineering, to hold that standard across the entire customer base. The Role CRE is a rapid response team and a proactive engineering team. You fix things at the edge as they come up, and you help build the product capabilities that identify customer issues before they become a crisis. Both modes are equally core. Rapid response. When a customer issue surfaces that is high-severity, cross-layer and complex, you are the engineer who answers. You reproduce the defect, isolate the root cause across Cloudflare's infrastructure and the customer's stack, drive the fix with Product Engineering, and confirm resolution. You hold on-call for high-severity incidents as part of a global shift rotation. Proactive engineering. When no fire is burning, you work with Product Engineering and our platform teams to build the capabilities that make the next fire cheaper or unnecessary: telemetry pipelines that correlate signals across the customer base, detectors that fire before a human notices, diagnostic tooling that scales across hundreds of customers, automation that reduces toil for Customer Support. Every incident you carry generates engineering output that reduces the cost of recurrence. The work compounds. Cloudflare is building CRE as an AI-native function. You will work with and help build agents and tooling that pre-diagnose incidents, surface relevant logs and configuration, and propose fixes with cited evidence. Drive the fix with Product Engineering. Partner with a government customer's SRE team during an active DDoS event. Help them shape their Magic Transit and WAF configuration in real time. The R2 Gateway team owns the request-facing layer of R2 — the S3-compatible API gateway that every object put, get, list, and delete flows through. Build and operate production services on Cloudflare Workers and Kubernetes that handle high-throughput request traffic with strong availability and durability guarantees. Own the request path end to end — authentication, authorization, routing, rate limiting, and error handling — and the interfaces between the gateway and R2's storage and metadata layers. Own projects end to end: from design docs through implementation, testing, deployment, and production monitoring. Continuously improve the reliability, performance, and observability of the gateway; ramp quickly into unfamiliar and legacy code paths and reduce operational toil. Available Locations | Austin, TX | New York, NY | San Francisco, CA or Seattle, WA About the Role The Cloudflare Hyperdrive team builds the technology that makes regional databases feel like they are global. Hyperdrive is a core piece of the Cloudflare Developer Platform that accelerates database queries from Cloudflare Workers by pooling connections and caching data at the edge. By eliminating the massive latency overhead of TCP, TLS, and database-specific handshakes, Hyperdrive allows developers to use the databases they already know and love—like PostgreSQL and MySQL—without the "cold start" performance penalties typically associated with serverless environments. Responsibilities Hyperdrive is integrated directly into the Cloudflare global network and features: Global Connection Pooling: Maintains "warm" connections to origin databases across the globe, reducing connection times by up to 90%. Intelligent Query Caching: Automatically caches frequently run read queries as close to the user as possible. Protocol-Aware Proxying: Features custom-built implementations of database wire protocols (PostgreSQL and MySQL) to parse and optimize traffic in real-time. Seamless Integration: Works with existing ORMs and drivers, providing a simple connection string that "just works" for developers. The team is geographically distributed across North America. You will own your code from inception to release, delivering solutions at all layers of the software stack to empower Cloudflare customers. On any given day, you might write a design document that outlines how you plan to solve a specific problem, or fix a bug in how our user experience renders. You can expect to interact with a variety of languages and technologies including, but not limited to Rust, Go, C++, Typescript. Desirable Skills, Knowledge, and Experience You have 5+ years of professional experience with Rust, Go, or C++. You understand how to write code that respects CPU and memory constraints. You are comfortable with the Linux networking stack. You know your way around TCP/IP, TLS, and WebSockets. You don’t just use databases; you understand how they work. You’re familiar with connection lifecycles, transaction states, and wire protocols. You enjoy the challenge of debugging complex, distributed systems and building for "five nines" reliability. Bonus Points Experience with PgBouncer, ProxySQL, or custom database middleware. Familiarity with the Cloudflare Workers ecosystem and the unique stateful connection challenges of ephemeral computing. You’ve contributed to database drivers, ORMs, or low-level networking libraries. Experience using eBPF, perf, or other profiling tools to find and kill bottlenecks. descriptionAr: We're hiring a Compensation Lead to build Perplexity's compensation function and own its day-to-day execution. You'll build the programs and processes that support how we hire, recognize, and retain people. You should be comfortable moving between program design and an individual offer, building longer-term structure while keeping today's decisions moving. The goal is a compensation approach that is competitive, financially sound, and clear enough for people to use, without adding unnecessary complexity. What you'll own Build the compensation foundation. Assess existing practices, data, and tools; prioritize the gaps; and develop recommendations on compensation philosophy, market positioning, and cash and equity guidelines. Develop salary ranges and market benchmarks. Establish a consistent approach to pricing roles across functions and locations. Partner with People and business leaders on job scope and leveling, and explain where market data is useful or incomplete. Own day-to-day compensation decisions. Be the primary partner for offers, promotions, pay adjustments, and compensation questions. Evaluate recommendations against market data, internal equity, and budget, with clear approval paths for exceptions. Design and run compensation reviews. Build the calendar, planning models, manager guidance, and approval process. Coordinate with Finance, People Operations, Payroll, and equity partners to carry decisions through to accurate implementation. Inform leadership decisions. Model the cost and employee impact of proposed changes to salary and equity programs. Present a recommendation and its trade-offs, then own execution once approved. Identify and address inconsistencies. Assess pay compression and potential inequities across teams, levels, and locations. Partner with People leadership and Legal on appropriate reviews and recommend actions. Build processes people can use. Establish decision records, recruiter and manager guidance, and clear explanations of compensation programs. Improve recurring workflows so consistent decisions don't depend on individual knowledge or one-off conversations. Own the data and tools behind the work. Establish reliable compensation records, select and manage benchmarking resources, and improve reporting and quality checks. Use approved automation and AI tools where they help, with appropriate protection for employee information and verification of results. What you bring Experience building compensation programs: You've established or substantially rebuilt compensation frameworks and processes with limited infrastructure, and stayed accountable for running them after launch. Technical compensation depth: Hands-on experience with market pricing, salary ranges, cash and equity programs, compensation reviews, and individual pay recommendations. Strong analytical judgment: You can build and audit models, reconcile imperfect data, and explain your assumptions. You know when a benchmark is a useful comparison and when it misses the role. Ability to influence decisions: You can turn analysis into a clear recommendation, discuss trade-offs with leadership, and constructively challenge an approach that isn't working. Independent, hands-on execution: You can set priorities, build a workable process, and manage urgent requests without losing progress on longer-term work. You're comfortable being both the person designing the program and the person checking the data. Discretion and clear communication: You handle sensitive information carefully and explain compensation decisions in language that recruiters, managers, and employees can understand.

descriptionAr: About the Team OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. The Creative Partnerships team supports that mission by building trusted relationships with creators, experts, and organizations to help them explore valuable uses of AI. We work across OpenAI to develop partnerships grounded in trust, usefulness, and measurable impact. Our work goes beyond individual launches and includes product education, partner feedback, and collaborative programs that create lasting value for partners and OpenAI. About the Role We’re looking for an experienced partnerships leader to develop and scale high-touch onboarding and enablement experiences for creators, brands and institutions. You will help partners move from initial curiosity to meaningful, hands-on use of OpenAI’s products. This includes understanding their work and ambitions, designing tailored onboarding experiences, helping them develop authentic use cases, and ensuring they have the support needed to engage confidently over time. You will serve as a trusted bridge between external partners and teams across OpenAI. You’ll translate product capabilities into relevant creative possibilities, bring actionable feedback and cultural insights back to the company, and develop an operating model that combines highly personalized support with the systems needed to scale. In this role, you will: Define the strategy, partner journey, operating model, and quality bar for high-touch onboarding, creating clear pathways from introduction and education to experimentation, adoption, and long-term engagement. Design and lead tailored onboarding sessions, workshops, product demonstrations, and ongoing enablement that help creators, brands, institutions and their teams apply OpenAI’s products to their work. Learn how each partner works and develop authentic use cases aligned with their creative goals, audiences, and values, helping turn early experimentation into compelling examples of creativity, expression, and connection. Serve as a consistent, trusted point of contact for partners and their representatives, anticipating needs, resolving challenges, and providing thoughtful support with discretion, care, and sound judgment. Partner with internal teams to explore broader collaborations where there is strong mutual value and authentic alignment. Bring actionable product feedback, emerging behaviors, creative workflows, and cultural insights to Product, Research, Marketing, Communications, Policy, and other teams. Help stakeholders understand partner needs and identify recurring opportunities or friction points that could inform product development and company strategy. Create feedback loops that show partners how their perspectives are heard and acted upon. Develop playbooks, enablement materials, partner briefs, follow-up plans, escalation paths, and reusable resources that balance personalized engagement with repeatable systems. Establish clear ownership and handoffs across Partnerships, Product, Marketing, Communications, Legal, Policy, and Support as the program scales. Define and track meaningful measures of success, including partner engagement, time to activation, depth of use, relationship health, actionable product feedback, and partnership outcomes. Use qualitative and quantitative insights to improve, expand, and scale the program. You might thrive in this role if you: Have 10+ years of experience in creator or talent partnerships, strategic partnerships, platform partnerships, product enablement, client services, or another highly relationship-driven field. Have experience supporting creators, brands, or other high-profile partners and their representatives. Build exceptional relationships through the judgment, discretion, and responsiveness required to earn trust over time. Bring strong cultural fluency and a nuanced understanding of how creators, talent, platforms, and communities influence one another. Translate complex or emerging technology into clear, relevant, and inspiring possibilities for non-technical audiences. Develop authentic use cases around a partner’s real goals rather than applying a one-size-fits-all approach. Align cross-functional stakeholders, manage dependencies, and create clarity in ambiguous environments. Communicate and facilitate effectively, whether leading intimate working sessions or engaging senior and high-profile audiences. Bring hands-on fluency with AI products and curiosity about how they can support creative work, expression, and connection. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X . We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do. You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity. The Opportunity: Grafana Labs is looking for a technically fluent engineer who loves building powerful demos, explaining complex systems clearly, and helping SRE and platform engineering leaders understand the value of our open approach to observability. As Grafana’s offering shifts from dashboards to industry-leading agentic observability, our Product Marketing team is responsible for closing the gap between what our products can do and how customers understand that value. That means building clear, consistent positioning, enabling sellers with trustworthy technical narratives, and creating content that helps Platform Engineering teams quickly grasp why Grafana Cloud is the right choice for them. As a Technical Product Marketer you will play a critical part in that transformation. You’ll be the hands-on engineer who brings our technical story to life for buyers, not just practitioners. You’ll build core demos, run technical workshops and webinars, and act as the technical bridge between our Product and Sales orgs. Your work will help SRE and platform engineering leaders evaluate Grafana with confidence, equip sales engineers with better tools and talk tracks, and ensure our technical value shows up clearly and consistently across the entire customer journey. This is a unique chance to shape how Grafana tells its story as we evolve our positioning in the AI era, strengthen seller enablement, and build a repeatable system for communicating product value. Record high-quality technical demo videos and walkthroughs in partnership with our video and content teams. Lead webinars, workshops, and technical sessions designed for evaluators. Teach customers not just how Grafana works, but why our approach is differentiated and valuable. Use AI tools to generate variations, summaries, and reusable assets that scale technical content across channels. Enable Solutions (Sales) Engineers with clear, consistent technical storytelling Serve as PMM’s technical liaison to the SE org, ensuring consistent messaging and demo guidance. Produce technical enablement assets, value-driven talk tracks, competitive narratives, and demo best practices. Help SEs and sellers communicate Grafana’s story with clarity, confidence, and differentiation. Collaborate with PMMs to drive technical buyer engagement across high-impact channels Partner with PMMs to identify the most important buyer personas, problems, and technical messages, and help shape the content strategy needed to reach them. Extend technical narratives into impactful buyer-facing channels including analyst briefings (Gartner, Forrester), industry forums, podcasts, conferences, and online technical communities. Bring a technical perspective to PMM planning—helping ensure our content, campaigns, and enablement reflect the real challenges and priorities of SREs and engineering leaders. Use automation & AI to scale technical content Partner with software engineers to streamline demo setup, content workflows, and asset updates through workflows, agents, scripts, and AI-driven tools. Use automation to make technical content more repeatable, discoverable, and scalable across teams. What Makes You a Great Fit: 5+ years in a technical role (solutions engineering, SRE, DevOps, backend engineering, technical PMM, or similar). Interest and ability to travel to training and customer events 10-12 weeks per year. Strong understanding of observability concepts and the needs of SRE/platform teams. Ability to translate deep technical concepts into clear, value-focused stories. Experience presenting technical content through demos, workshops, or webinars. Excellent written and verbal communication, with a crisp, structured, persuasive style. Strong cross-functional collaboration; comfort working with PMM, Product, SEs, DevRel, and Field Engineering. descriptionAr: Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X . We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do. You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity. The Opportunity: We’re looking for an enthusiastic, tech-forward product marketer to grow our Observability products by boldly positioning them and running campaigns to attract, convert and retain customers. As a Senior Product Marketing Manager, you will be in charge of the messaging and positioning for a broad product area. Then you’ll work closely with product managers and the marketing team to deliver campaigns, content, events, and training that help buyers buy (and sellers sell) our value. Product Marketing lives within the Product org rather than the Marketing org at Grafana Labs, and we think differently about the job. Rather than purely executing launches or campaigns, we want PMMs to teach product managers and engineers in our org how to think about growth and demand, and to codify product marketing knowledge into AI-forward tools and processes that anyone in the organization can use. For example, we all contribute product information to a shared knowledge base, which we use to generate enablement materials and decks. Grafana Labs is a fast-paced and growing organization. As such, this role requires strategic skills, an interest in teaching, and hands-on tactical execution (blogs, webinar outlines, video scripts, etc). Our team is full of people who crave impact and independence - if you are seeking a role with narrow scope where you run a defined playbook, this is not the job for you. What You'll Be Doing: Actively partner with and teach product managers to define product value, messaging, and go-to-market strategy, from competitive positioning to sales enablement collateral. Partner with product management, engineering and various go-to-market functions to create materials that help customers evaluate and adopt our products: reference architectures, implementation guides, detailed product information and more. Own customer lifecycle campaigns (competitive positioning, retention, upsell/cross-sell) to strategically shape marketing programs and drive growth across the entire customer journey. Conduct market and customer research to understand pain points, competition and opportunities. Teach go-to-market and sales teams our products’ capabilities and the value they provide, deliver training and enablement, ensure customer facing teams are able to effectively engage with customers, partners, and prospects. What Makes You a Great Fit: 4+ years of relevant experience (product marketing, solutions marketing, product management) Experience with marketing and selling to a technical audience A passion for open source, cloud native, and infrastructure technologies  Proven ability to take on complex projects and efficiently drive them from start to finish Ability to clearly articulate the value of technical products to customers and sellers alike Experience leading product or feature launches autonomously as well as part of a team Experience working with AI tools like ChatGPT and Claude to automate messaging and workflows Comfort working with a variety of internal and external stakeholders in complicated processes Strong product and technical curiosity that translate to clear packaging, positioning, and messaging Demonstrated quantitative analytical skills for analyzing campaign performance, evaluating lifecycle metrics, and making data-driven recommendations. Exceptional writing and communication skills A high “say-do” ratio in executing and delivering impact  Compensation & Rewards: In the US, the base compensation range for this role is $162,275 - $194,730. Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed throughout the interview process. All of our roles include Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), giving every team member ownership in Grafana Labs' success. We believe in shared outcomes—RSUs help us stay aligned and invested as we scale globally. *Compensation ranges are country specific. If you are applying for this role from a different location than listed above, your recruiter will discuss your specific market’s defined pay range & benefits at the beginning of the process. Promptly escalate government, court, law enforcement, and legal-threat requests according to approved procedures. Respond to routine requests using Legal-approved templates and guidance. Escalate matters requiring legal interpretation or disclosure of user information. Answer routine requests for information under Legal's guidance. Gather account history and draft responses for matters that need review. Help GRC process data subject requests and meet deadlines. Follow approved identity-verification and data-handling procedures. Coordinate security questionnaires and data protection agreements, with Legal and GRC responsible for substantive review and approval. Track each case through completion, including after handoffs. descriptionAr: About the Team We build software that helps understand and reduce risks from increasingly capable AI systems. Our work spans cybersecurity, frontier-risk evaluations, and red teaming, with a focus on turning research and testing into practical tools and reliable systems. We collaborate across research, engineering, and security to investigate model capabilities, identify potential failures, and develop ways to evaluate and improve safeguards. About the Role We’re looking for a Software Engineer to build the tools and infrastructure that support this work. You’ll partner closely with researchers and other engineers to translate evolving questions into useful software—from early prototypes to systems that teams can depend on. Projects may include backend services, evaluation infrastructure, data pipelines, and internal applications for running tests, investigating model behavior, and reviewing results. This is a general software engineering role with room to contribute across the stack and develop deeper expertise in AI safety and security. In this role, you will: Design, build, and maintain software that supports cybersecurity research, frontier-risk evaluations, and red teaming. Develop tools and workflows that make it easier to run evaluations, inspect results, and investigate failures. Build services, APIs, data pipelines, and interfaces that help researchers work efficiently. Turn experimental workflows into reusable, well-tested, and documented systems. Own projects from understanding the problem and designing a solution through implementation, deployment, and ongoing operation. Improve reliability, performance, observability, security, and usability as needs evolve. Collaborate with researchers, security specialists, and engineers to identify useful problems and make practical technical decisions. You might thrive in this role if you: Have strong software engineering fundamentals and experience building, shipping, and maintaining production software. Are proficient in a general-purpose programming language and comfortable learning unfamiliar tools and systems. Have experience in one or more areas such as backend development, full-stack applications, infrastructure, or data systems. Can take an open-ended problem, clarify what matters, and deliver a useful solution. Balance rapid iteration with maintainable design and operational reliability. Communicate clearly and enjoy working with people across technical disciplines. Are interested in understanding advanced AI systems and helping address their risks. Experience with security, developer tools, research infrastructure, evaluation platforms, distributed systems, or AI applications would be valuable. Prior AI research or cybersecurity experience is helpful but not required. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement . Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. For unincorporated Los Angeles County workers: we reasonably believe that criminal history may have a direct, adverse and negative relationship with the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of a conditional offer of employment: protect computer hardware entrusted to you from theft, loss or damage; return all computer hardware in your possession (including the data contained therein) upon termination of employment or end of assignment; and maintain the confidentiality of proprietary, confidential, and non-public information. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations. To notify OpenAI that you believe this job posting is non-compliant, please submit a report through this form . No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made via this link . OpenAI Global Applicant Privacy Policy At OpenAI, we believe artificial intelligence has the potential to help people solve immense global challenges, and we want the upside of AI to be widely shared. Join us in shaping the future of technology.

descriptionAr: Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X . We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do. You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity. About Grafana Labs:  There are more than 700,000 active installations of Grafana around the globe, monitoring everything from beehives to climate change in the Alps. The instantly recognizable dashboards have been spotted everywhere from a SpaceX launch and Minecraft HQ to Wimbledon and the Tour de France. Grafana Labs also helps companies including Bloomberg, JPMorgan Chase, and eBay manage their observability strategies with full-stack offerings that can be run fully managed with Grafana Cloud, or self-managed with Grafana Enterprise Stack. The Grafana stack has grown to include more open-source projects, including Grafana Loki (for logs) and Grafana Tempo (for traces) and Grafana Mimir (for metrics). Description of Duties We’re looking for a Staff Technical Writer to create documentation and learning content that helps people adopt and master Grafana’s observability products. You’ll work with engineers, product managers, and the Grafana writing team to produce content for a range of products and audiences, from first-time users to experienced practitioners. Because our products and priorities evolve, we’re looking for someone who learns new technical domains quickly. AI is part of how this team works. We use AI-assisted workflows and tools throughout the content lifecycle, from research and drafting to review, validation, and maintenance. You’ll use these tools every day and help the team get better at using them. Key Responsibilities Plan, research, write, and maintain documentation and learning content (concepts, tasks, tutorials, references, and in-product learning) that supports adoption and long-term product mastery. Use AI tools and workflows to work faster and at a higher quality: drafting, structuring, technical validation, consistency checks, and keeping content current. You apply human judgment to everything AI produces and take responsibility for its accuracy. Contribute to the team’s shared AI workflows and skills, and look for ways to improve and automate how we create and maintain content as tools and models evolve. Partner with engineers, PMs, and other stakeholders to understand product requirements, interview subject matter experts, and turn complex technical detail into clear, accurate content. Test what you document. Run the software, follow your own procedures, and flag product and UX gaps you find along the way. Let data guide your priorities. We have strong docs and learning analytics. You’ll use them, along with user feedback, to find content gaps, prioritize your work, and show the impact of what you ship. Work with the documentation manager and other writers to improve information architecture, voice, and consistency across our docs, and to make information easy to find for both people and AI-driven search and assistants. Manage several projects at once, using judgment to prioritize and communicate clearly when the plan changes. Mentor teammates and share practices that raise the quality of the team’s work. Requirements What experience would make someone be successful in this role? Experience writing or documenting enterprise or developer-facing software, with a portfolio or writing samples that show technical depth. Hands-on experience using AI tools and models in your writing workflow (such as LLM assistants, agentic coding tools, or custom prompts and skills), and the ability to explain how you evaluate and verify their output. Experience working with docs-as-code: command-line Git, GitHub (pull requests and reviews), Markdown, and common IDEs. Comfort working in technical environments. You can set up, run, and troubleshoot software yourself to verify what you write (for example, command line, containers, or Kubernetes, or a willingness to learn quickly). Experience collaborating with engineers and product managers to get accurate technical information. Experience working remotely and asynchronously on a distributed team. What you’ll bring to the role Curiosity about AI as a craft. You treat AI workflows as a professional skill. You experiment, share what works, and know where AI helps and where it doesn’t. Technical credibility. You care about accuracy, you learn new technical domains quickly, and you ask questions until you understand them. Strong judgment and editing skills. You can tell good content from plausible-sounding content, and you hold the line on quality. Ownership. You manage multiple projects and work well both independently and collaboratively. Clarity. You write concisely and plainly for readers of all experience levels. Bonus: Experience with observability, monitoring, or cloud-native tooling, or con

descriptionAr: Perplexity is looking for a senior commercial attorney to join our Legal team. We are looking for an independent, business-practical yet diligent-minded professional who can carry live deals, extend the infrastructure we have already built, and hold the line on the terms that matter as deal volume, complexity, and regulatory surface all grow. You will negotiate directly with large enterprise customers across a large variety of industries including financial services, healthcare, government, and other regulated industries, partner daily with Enterprise Sales, Partnerships, Deal Desk, Security, Privacy, Product, and Finance, and advise on the legal questions that come with agentic, retrieval, and API products deployed inside enterprise environments. This is a high-impact, hands-on role for someone who is genuinely a self starter. This role is for you if you get energy from ambiguous, first‑of‑their‑kind problems and enjoy designing repeatable approaches that scale. You default to enabling the business, frame risk in practical terms, and focus on durable structures rather than one‑off fixes. Responsibilities Independently lead end-to-end drafting, review, and negotiation of Enterprise customer agreements across our suite of offerings: Enterprise Pro, Enterprise Max, Computer, and API product lines, including MSAs, order forms, SaaS and API terms, DPAs, BAAs, security exhibits, customer-paper redlines, product-specific addenda, and public-sector vehicles such as GSA MAS orders and federal RFP responses. Serve as a trusted legal partner to Enterprise Sales, Partnerships, Deal Desk, and Customer Success, providing fast, practical, business-aligned counsel that accelerates deal velocity, protects the terms that matter, and scales as the Sales organization grows. Extend and maintain the existing Enterprise negotiation playbook, DPA and Privacy Notice architecture, product-specific term libraries, and fallback positions as our product surface, customer mix, and regulatory environment evolve, so that positions compound into reusable precedent rather than being re-litigated deal by deal. Advise on AI-specific contract terms for enterprise deployments, including bespoke data postures; negotiate output ownership and liability, agentic-feature risk allocation and translate product operations into enterprise contract commitments. Partner cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, Security, Privacy, Finance, and Compliance to surface and address legal risk early, particularly on customer-data flows, enterprise integrations, model routing, and customer-specific compliance requirements. Monitor the evolving regulatory landscape for enterprise AI, data protection, and public-sector procurement (GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, HIPAA, DORA, EU AI Act, sector-specific frameworks) and translate emerging requirements into practical contractual positions and updated playbook guidance. Represent Perplexity Legal externally on customer negotiation calls with counterparty counsel at sophisticated enterprises. What we are looking for Exceptional communicator who owns deadlines, proactively manages internal and external expectations, and escalates early and clearly to protect deal timelines and momentum. A proactive problem‑solver who defaults to “yes, and” when engaging with internal stakeholders: you look for ways to make deals work, frame risk clearly, and design long‑term, scalable solutions. A disciplined drafter who favors surgical, minimal‑footprint edits over wholesale rewrites, grounds positions in documented rationale, and preserves material legal meaning and risk allocation under time pressure. Someone who can articulate complex legal risk and concepts in the form of simple, actionable terms for non‑legal stakeholders, leads with practical “how to make this work” advice, and designs creative, long‑term solutions to novel, cutting‑edge challenges. Someone genuinely excited by novel, cutting‑edge challenges in AI products and the commercial and regulatory questions they surface, and who enjoys turning ambiguity into clear, reusable approaches. Qualifications JD and in good standing with an active U.S. state bar membership. At least 7+ years of combined law firm and in-house experience, with a substantial in-house component, and a demonstrated track record of independently owning complex enterprise SaaS or API deals from the vendor side, including work with regulated-industry customers (financial services, healthcare, or government). Experience advising on commercial terms and pricing structures for high‑growth SaaS/API businesses, including usage‑based and tiered pricing, pilots, and expansion frameworks. Our mission is to make powerful AI easier to access, its value easier to understand, and new ways of using it easier to bring to market. We work where product experience, platform architecture, and business strategy meet. A new plan or pricing model can change what customers can accomplish—and requires careful engineering across eligibility, entitlements, usage, and subscriptions. We turn that complexity into capabilities that product teams can build on and experiences that customers can trust. Working with Product, Design, Finance, Financial Engineering, and Data Science, we’re shaping a platform that can evolve alongside our models and products. This is an opportunity to help define a new team’s technical direction and build systems that expand what OpenAI can offer. About the Role We’re looking for experienced Staff+ and Senior engineers who combine full-stack product instincts with strong backend and systems depth. You’ll help decide what to build, establish the architecture, and carry ideas through to working products—from a customer’s first interaction with a plan to the services that determine what they can access and use. The work spans new pricing and packaging capabilities, plan and usage experiences, and the shared UIs and tools that make launches repeatable. You’ll partner closely with Financial Engineering to connect these capabilities to subscription and billing systems, keeping customer access and state consistent as offerings evolve. You’ll have substantial ownership over technical decisions and delivery in an area where the roadmap is still taking shape. Your impact will show up in the experiences you ship, the engineering work you eliminate from future launches, and the opportunities your systems make possible. In this role, you will: Define and build shared pricing and packaging capabilities, including plan configuration, eligibility, entitlement integrations, and usage allowances. Create intuitive plan and usage experiences across the stack, connecting polished interfaces to product APIs and backend services. Turn new commercial ideas into working prototypes and experiments with Product, Finance, and Data Science, then use what you learn to guide the next iteration. Design integrations with Financial Engineering that preserve correct access and subscription state through plan changes, migrations, asynchronous updates, and partial failures. Build reusable components and configuration tools that let teams launch offerings with less custom engineering and fewer dependencies. Take responsibility for production quality through migration planning, staged rollouts, testing, monitoring, and recovery paths. Shape the technical roadmap, make clear tradeoffs between immediate launches and shared foundations, and develop other engineers through code and design reviews. You might thrive in this role if you: Have set architectural direction and delivered significant projects involving multiple teams, while remaining an active contributor to the code. Bring depth in backend or distributed systems and can work across the APIs and interfaces that turn those systems into useful products. Reason rigorously about data models, lifecycle transitions, consistency, concurrency, and what happens when an operation fails or runs twice. Have taken loosely defined customer or business problems through discovery, implementation, and production operation. Combine product intuition with experimentation and analysis, and care about whether customers understand and benefit from what you build. Enjoy establishing new capabilities: choosing an initial design, shipping something useful, and improving it as the problem becomes clearer. Build alignment across disciplines, explain technical choices clearly, and help teammates take on greater responsibility. Experience with pricing, subscriptions, entitlements, usage-based products, billing integrations, or growth platforms would be especially valuable. We also welcome engineers whose experience building demanding product or platform systems prepares them to learn this domain. descriptionAr: Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X . We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do. You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity. The Opportunity  Grafana's Demand Generation team creates and accelerates pipeline across the full customer journey. We run a modern, AI-forward operation: lifecycle email programs driven by an AI engine, territory-level buying signals surfaced directly to sales leaders, and agentic workflows that handle work that used to take teams of specialists. Our webinar program is one of the highest-leverage things we run: technical, practitioner-first sessions on a weekly cadence across AMER, EMEA, APAC and LATAM, putting the product in front of the people who would actually use it. Hands-on sessions, not sales pitches. We're hiring a Webinar Program Manager to own it. This is a specialist seat, not a generalist one. You'll inherit an established program with a documented process and a full handover from the person who built it, and you'll own the operating rhythm from there: the calendar, the presenters, the build and promotion of every session, the follow-up, and the reporting. This is not a "run the playbook" role. Sessions run in parallel at a pace no one could manage by hand, so the way to raise quality is to keep automating the mechanics. We expect this person to build with AI as a default and treat automation as a first-class deliverable, not a side project. You'd be joining a demand gen team that is genuinely rebuilding how the function works, where AI agents run real production programs and the people on the team design the machine rather than turn the crank. The webinar program already produces, and much of the pipeline it touches starts with a session rather than a seller. You're not here to prove webinars matter. You're here to make each one produce more with less manual work behind it. What You'll Be Doing Own the webinar calendar end to end. Presenter booking, registration pages, campaign setup, promotion, live delivery, follow-up, and the flip to on-demand, across multiple regions and time zones. Keep sessions practitioner-first. Brief technical presenters, shape the outline, and keep a session useful to the audience that registered for it. Bring data to topic planning. Use past performance and downstream pipeline quality to recommend what we run and what we retire, and lock the plan with demand gen and product marketing each quarter. Automate the production line. Extend the automation behind session setup and promotion, and keep pushing into the parts of the process a person shouldn't be doing by hand, including repurposing recordings into other content. Report on what happens after the session. Registrations are the input. Connect sessions to product adoption and pipeline, report it honestly, and flag what isn't producing. Grow the program's reach. Expand into additional languages and formats where the numbers justify it. What Makes You a Great Fit 4+ years in demand generation, event marketing, or lifecycle marketing at a B2B software company (open source or developer-focused a plus). Hands-on ownership of a recurring webinar or virtual event calendar across multiple regions. A cadence you were accountable for hitting, not a handful of one-off sessions. Hands-on with a webinar platform (ON24, Zoom Webinars, Contrast, Goldcast or similar) and the plumbing behind it: CRM campaigns, registration sync, attendance data, follow-up triggers. Comfortable working with technical presenters. You can brief an engineer or solutions architect and hold the line on what the audience came for. Hands-on with AI in your actual work: you've built automations or agentic workflows (or are visibly on that path), and you think about AI as leverage, not a threat or a buzzword. Comfortable with data: you can pull your own numbers, sanity-check them, and build a program readout a VP would trust. Strong program management fundamentals. Twenty-plus moving pieces at once is a logistics job before it's a marketing job, and you ship on time without needing a coordinator. Bonus Points For Content repurposing at scale: clips, blog, social, on-demand libraries. Localized program experience, and a view on when translation earns its cost. Familiarity with the observability, monitoring or open source ecosystem. Customer.io, Salesforce and a modern data stack (BigQuery or similar). Experience with product-led motions alongside sales-led ones. In Canada, the base compensation range for this role is CAD 101,000   - CAD 122,000 .  Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed throughout the interview process. descriptionAr: About the Team The IT System Operations Team provides engineering and operational expertise to the OpenAI IT organization. The team ensures that employee-facing systems, identity workflows, and enterprise applications operate in a predictable, governed, and continuously reliable manner as the organization scales. The Enterprise Platforms pod runs the SaaS applications employees rely on to communicate, collaborate, and manage work. The pod owns application administration, configuration, integrations, operational controls, and complex escalations. We work across Google Workspace, GCP, Slack, Atlassian and service-management tools, ChatGPT Enterprise, and other enterprise applications, partnering with IT Support, Systems Engineering, Identity & Access Foundations, Security, and business teams. About the Role We’re looking for an IT Systems Engineer to join our Enterprise Platforms pod, with deep experience in platforms such as Google Workspace, Google Cloud Platform (GCP), and Slack, and a focus on application integration, automation, and internal tools. You’ll connect services across the application portfolio, build tools that simplify work for employees and IT, and own improvements from discovery and design through implementation, rollout, and ongoing operation. The goal is to reduce repeated manual administration and build reusable capability for user migrations, M&A integrations, and broader enterprise platform work. Infrastructure as code is central to how you’ll work. You’ll use Terraform, version control, code review, and automated delivery pipelines as the default approach to managing platform configuration and supporting infrastructure. You’ll pair that foundation with APIs and code to build integrations and tools, simplify administrative workflows, and turn recurring issues into durable engineering improvements. You’ll work across collaboration platforms, cloud integrations, service-management workflows, and ChatGPT Enterprise administration. You’ll also participate in on-call and end-user escalations, helping restore service and improve the systems employees depend on. In this role, you will: Engineer and operate enterprise platforms through infrastructure as code, using Terraform to manage supported configuration, access, and controls. Build reusable modules, bring existing resources under management, and detect and reconcile configuration drift. Use APIs and automation for capabilities outside provider coverage. Design, build, and maintain integrations across enterprise applications and cloud services. Own data flows, API access, OAuth clients, service accounts, error handling, and operational monitoring. Partner with cloud and security owners on project setup, permissions, credential handling, and technical handoffs. Build and improve enterprise application integrations and Jira/service-management workflows for IT, Security, and business teams. Translate operational needs into maintainable configurations, routing, approvals, and automation. Develop ChatGPT Enterprise workspace administration using APIs and infrastructure as code. Test administrative capabilities and provide Customer Zero feedback to product teams based on real operational needs. Build reusable internal tools, automation, and autonomous workflows across the enterprise application portfolio, including self-service workflows, administrative utilities, and cross-application processes that support routine operations and user migrations. Use code, APIs, infrastructure as code, and AI or agent workflows with testing, error handling, logging, documentation, and clear boundaries for privileged actions. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X . If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity. About Grafana Labs:  There are more than 700,000 active installations of Grafana around the globe, monitoring everything from beehives to climate change in the Alps. The instantly recognizable dashboards have been spotted everywhere from a SpaceX launch and Minecraft HQ to Wimbledon and the Tour de France. Grafana Labs also helps companies including Bloomberg, JPMorgan Chase, and eBay manage their observability strategies with full-stack offerings that can be run fully managed with Grafana Cloud, or self-managed with Grafana Enterprise Stack. The Grafana stack has grown to include more open-source projects, including Grafana Loki (for logs) and Grafana Tempo (for traces) and Grafana Mimir (for metrics). Description of Duties We’re looking for a Staff Technical Writer to create documentation and learning content that helps people adopt and master Grafana’s observability products. You’ll work with engineers, product managers, and the Grafana writing team to produce content for a range of products and audiences, from first-time users to experienced practitioners. Because our products and priorities evolve, we’re looking for someone who learns new technical domains quickly. AI is part of how this team works. We use AI-assisted workflows and tools throughout the content lifecycle, from research and drafting to review, validation, and maintenance. You’ll use these tools every day and help the team get better at using them. Key Responsibilities Plan, research, write, and maintain documentation and learning content (concepts, tasks, tutorials, references, and in-product learning) that supports adoption and long-term product mastery. Use AI tools and workflows to work faster and at a higher quality: drafting, structuring, technical validation, consistency checks, and keeping content current. You apply human judgment to everything AI produces and take responsibility for its accuracy. Contribute to the team’s shared AI workflows and skills, and look for ways to improve and automate how we create and maintain content as tools and models evolve. Partner with engineers, PMs, and other stakeholders to understand product requirements, interview subject matter experts, and turn complex technical detail into clear, accurate content. Test what you document. Run the software, follow your own procedures, and flag product and UX gaps you find along the way. Let data guide your priorities. We have strong docs and learning analytics. You’ll use them, along with user feedback, to find content gaps, prioritize your work, and show the impact of what you ship. Work with the documentation manager and other writers to improve information architecture, voice, and consistency across our docs, and to make information easy to find for both people and AI-driven search and assistants. Manage several projects at once, using judgment to prioritize and communicate clearly when the plan changes. Mentor teammates and share practices that raise the quality of the team’s work. Requirements What experience would make someone be successful in this role? Experience writing or documenting enterprise or developer-facing software, with a portfolio or writing samples that show technical depth. Hands-on experience using AI tools and models in your writing workflow (such as LLM assistants, agentic coding tools, or custom prompts and skills), and the ability to explain how you evaluate and verify their output. Experience working with docs-as-code: command-line Git, GitHub (pull requests and reviews), Markdown, and common IDEs. Comfort working in technical environments. You can set up, run, and troubleshoot software yourself to verify what you write (for example, command line, containers, or Kubernetes, or a willingness to learn quickly). Experience collaborating with engineers and product managers to get accurate technical information. Experience working remotely and asynchronously on a distributed team. What you’ll bring to the role Curiosity about AI as a craft. You treat AI workflows as a professional skill. You experiment, share what works, and know where AI helps and where it doesn’t. Technical credibility. You care about accuracy, you learn new technical domains quickly, and you ask questions until you understand them. Strong judgment and editing skills. You can tell good content from plausible-sounding content, and you hold the line on quality. Ownership. You manage multiple projects and work well both independently and collaboratively. Clarity. You write concisely and plainly for readers of all experience levels. Bonus: Experience with observability, monitoring, or cloud-native tooling, or con

Sales Development sits at the front of this motion—where technical curiosity becomes executive engagement and OpenAI’s enterprise relationships begin. This is a foundational front-line leadership role within OpenAI’s enterprise GTM organization. You will partner closely with Sales, Marketing, Solutions Engineering, Partnerships, and Strategy & Operations to drive pipeline generation and help shape the future of OpenAI’s enterprise growth engine. Please note this role is based in Dublin with office attendance required 3 days a week. account-based motions, and product-led signals Establish strong operational rigor around activity metrics, conversion rates, pipeline quality, and execution consistency Partner closely with Account continuous improvement Work cross-functionally with Marketing, Partnerships, Solutions Engineering, and Strategy & Operations to optimize pipeline generation efforts Support hiring, onboarding, and ramping of new SDR talent as the organization scales Bring market feedback and customer insights back into the broader GTM organization You may thrive in this role if you Have 6–10+ years of experience and overachievement in sales, business development, or GTM roles, with at least 3+ years in management Bring experience managing SDRs or business development teams in enterprise SaaS or platform businesses Have a strong understanding of enterprise prospecting, pipeline generation, and outbound strategy Are highly operational and data-driven, with experience managing metrics, Built on a semantic model, Omni gives teams a governed context graph, so everyone gets the same trusted answer. Ask in plain English, refine in workbooks, or bring your data into tools like Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and Slack. Our team has spent decades building data platforms, and we started Omni to fix problems we saw firsthand. Today, we help customers like Condé Nast, BambooHR, and Synthesia get better answers from their data. We're headquartered in San Francisco and have raised $217M from top investors including ICONIQ, Theory Ventures, and Redpoint Ventures. Our latest $120M Series C valued us at $1.5B. If you like helping people get more from their data, come build with us. We’d love to hear from you. The Role We're looking for a Head of Growth Marketing, EMEA to build and run the demand engine that generates pipeline across EMEA. You'll own the regional growth strategy, budget, and pipeline target, developing each market according to its stage. You'll lead a small team of growth marketers while building campaigns and programs yourself. You'll partner closely with EMEA sales leadership, BDRs, partnerships, and product marketing, and work with the Global Events team on flagship regional events. This role reports to the Director, Global Growth. Responsibilities Own the EMEA pipeline target. Set the regional growth strategy and plan against a pipeline number. Be accountable for marketing-sourced and influenced pipeline across every EMEA territory. Develop each market by its stage. Decide where to invest, where to test, and where to hold back across EMEA, and explain the tradeoffs to leadership. Run multi-channel programs hands-on. Plan and run localized campaigns, field events and executive dinners, conferences, ABM, partner co-marketing, and paid digital. Stay in the detail to make them work. Partner with EMEA sales leadership and BDRs. Agree territory priorities, target accounts, and ICP, and make sure programs turn into meetings and pipeline. Own and allocate the EMEA marketing budget. descriptionAr: About the Team The OpenAI Risk & Audit team is building an enterprise risk capability for a company operating at the frontier of AI. We help leaders identify, understand, and manage the risks that matter most while enabling responsible innovation and durable growth. We are developing a modern enterprise risk management (ERM) program and the technology foundation that powers it. Our work connects risk strategy, governance, compliance, and assurance with high-quality data, automated workflows, continuous monitoring, and AI-enabled analysis. We partner across Finance, Security, Legal, Engineering, Product, People, Operations, and Internal Audit, and provide clear reporting to senior leadership and the Board. We aim to make risk ownership practical, decision-useful, and embedded in how OpenAI builds and scales. About the Role As the Head of Enterprise Risk Management, you will help build and lead an integrated ERM program and the ERM platform that supports it. You will establish common risk language, governance, and decision processes while translating them into scalable systems, data products, and workflows. You will own enterprise risk assessments, maintain a centralized risk register, develop risk appetite and key risk indicators, and help leaders evaluate significant changes such as new products, markets, partnerships, major systems, and strategic investments. This is a senior individual contributor role for a hands-on leader who will build our ERM capability from the ground up, with the potential to build and lead a team over time. You will work with technical and business teams to connect source systems, improve data quality, automate evidence and control monitoring, and use AI to surface emerging risks and accelerate analysis. You will also help create a strong risk culture, coordinate assurance across the three lines, and communicate complex issues with clarity and sound judgment. Design plays a critical role in making powerful AI intuitive, useful, and trustworthy. We hold a high bar for quality and build experiences that earn users’ confidence, while moving quickly and learning from real-world feedback. We favor early validation and continuous refinement over waiting until every detail is perfect. About the Role We’re looking for a Product Designer to shape how startups, small businesses, and growing teams discover, adopt, and unlock lasting value from ChatGPT. You’ll own growth experiences across the customer journey, turning the potential of AI into meaningful, everyday impact for people across the world. This is a highly hands-on role for a designer who pairs exceptional craft with strong product judgment and an experimental mindset. You’ll tackle some of our most interesting growth challenges, using creativity, product intuition, and experimentation to discover new opportunities. We’re looking for someone who loves treating metrics as puzzles to solve, finding unexpected solutions, and learning quickly through iteration. Above all, you bring exceptional design craft and believe that driving measurable impact and building beautiful, intuitive experiences should go hand in hand. This role is based in our San Francisco HQ. We offer relocation assistance to new employees. In this role, you will: Own end-to-end design for growth experiences across ChatGPT Design and improve experiences across user lifecycle stages like discovery, onboarding, activation, engagement, collaboration, conversion, and retention. Turn ambiguous opportunities into clear hypotheses, compelling prototypes, and polished product experiences. Set a high bar for interaction design, visual craft, systems thinking, content, and end-to-end coherence. Partner closely with product, engineering, data science, research, and go-to-market teams to shape both strategy and execution. Use quantitative data, experimentation, research, and qualitative insights to identify opportunities and evaluate outcomes. Translate complex and rapidly evolving AI capabilities into approachable experiences for people with a wide range of technical expertise. Move fluidly between longer-term product vision and fast, iterative execution. Contribute reusable patterns and insights that strengthen growth experiences across ChatGPT. You might thrive in this role if you: Have a portfolio demonstrating exceptional product thinking, interaction design, and visual craft across complex, shipped products. Have led substantial product initiatives from early exploration through launch and iteration. Possess strong product judgment and can connect user needs, business goals, technical possibilities, and measurable outcomes. Are comfortable working with data and experiments while balancing quantitative signals with research, intuition, and design judgment. Can move quickly without compromising clarity, coherence, trust, or craft. Are fluent in using AI to explore, prototype, communicate, and extend what you can build. Can turn ambiguous, fast-moving problems into a clear point of view and actionable product direction. Communicate through strong narratives and prototypes that align cross-functional teams. Are excited to rethink established growth patterns and invent interactions that feel native to AI. Care deeply about building products that are useful, trustworthy, and worthy of users’ time. Direct experience in growth design or developer products is helpful but not required. We’re most interested in designers with strong product judgment, exceptional craft, and evidence that their work meaningfully changed user behavior or business outcomes. experience driving multi-product adoption, cross-sell, and upsell across a book of business Track record of pushing pace on input metrics, building repeatable playbooks, and optimizing systems and processes to improve team output Strong collaboration and influencing skills across Sales, Product, Operations, and other GTM teams; demonstrated ability to represent Customer Success at a leadership level Comfort with and curiosity about AI tools and their application to CS workflows; ability to lead a team through AI-driven process transformation and evaluate how AI can augment CSM productivity and customer outcomes Strong understanding of customer financial workflows, including AP/AR, spend controls, and month-end close processes; descriptionAr: About Ramp Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books. The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving. We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome. The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. About the Role As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you’ll solve the hardest problems standing between Ramp and the world’s largest and most complex companies — shaping and shipping the product capabilities that unlock our growth upmarket. You'll be part of our Core FDE org, which is an agent-first, high-pace, customer-facing engineering team. On FDE, you will interact directly with customers and deliver solutions end to end — understanding pain points, shaping product decisions, and building agents that autonomously expand Ramp's capabilities. Check out our Engineering Blog and FDE post for more context on our work! What You’ll Do Deliver software end to end that meet the needs of our largest customers — understanding user pain points, scoping product specs, and building agents that autonomously implement solutions. Collaborate closely with Sales, Solutions, Customer Success, and Account Management to close deals, activate customers, and expand the value Ramp provides over time. Drive the core product engineering roadmap through our embedding model — specializing within a core product area to develop deep domain expertise and make prioritization calls on when to build a custom solution vs. accelerate a broader initiative. What You Need 3+ years of software engineering experience preferred Extensive experience building with and for agents Track record of shipping high-quality products at scale Comfort and excitement to be customer-facing Desire to work in a fast-paced environment, continuously grow, and master your craft Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global) Flexible PTO Centralized home-office equipment ordering Health and wellness stipend Budget for intra-office travel Weekly coffee stipend United States 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents One Medical annual membership 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year) Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay Pet insurance In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed) Canada Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life Life, AD&D, and disability coverage Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime) Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP) Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health United Kingdom Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay Referral Instructions If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf. Other notices Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. Beware of recruiting scams: Ramp will only contact you through official @ Ramp.com email addresses and will never ask for payment or sensitive personal information during the hiring process. Ramp Applicant Privacy Notice

descriptionAr: About the Team The Business Marketing team helps businesses understand, adopt, and get value from OpenAI’s products. Partner Marketing brings that mission to life through the OpenAI Partner Network, helping partners communicate their value, demonstrate customer impact, and grow their businesses with OpenAI. We work closely with Partnerships, Sales, Product Marketing, Communications, and partner organizations to turn shared opportunities into programs that drive adoption, customer engagement, and measurable business results. About the Role We are hiring a Program Manager to build and scale partner storytelling, customer proof, and public-facing content programs for the OpenAI Partner Network. You will own the program strategy and end-to-end delivery, from identifying compelling customer outcomes and building partner relationships to developing case studies, whitepapers, webinars, and web content. A central responsibility is building a scalable partner customer reference program—from identifying promising stories and developing relationships to publishing case studies, whitepapers, and webinars. You will establish the processes, editorial standards, and distribution plans that make this work repeatable and build a trusted destination for partner-led customer stories. You will also shape OpenAI Partner Network website messaging and content, support partner launches and announcements. Across these efforts, you will prioritize the stories and programs with the greatest potential to support adoption, pipeline, and partner growth. This is a highly cross-functional individual contributor role with no people-management responsibility. It is built for someone who combines strategic judgment with hands-on execution: a curious storyteller who builds strong relationships, moves quickly, and turns ideas into finished work. This is a hybrid role, based in office three days a week at our San Francisco office. In this role, you will: Build and own the partner customer reference program. Establish a repeatable approach to sourcing, qualifying, developing, approving, and publishing customer stories with partners. Develop internal proof points that can mature into public references as customer readiness and permissions allow. Create compelling customer proof. Develop partner narratives and messaging. Synthesize technical, customer, and business information into clear positioning, thought leadership, and messages for internal and external audiences. Shape the OpenAI Partner Network’s web presence. Own website content strategy, messaging, and ongoing content development, working with Brand, Design, and web teams to communicate the network’s value and create a cohesive partner identity. Support partner launches and communications. Develop launch narratives, messaging, announcements, and supporting content in close partnership with Partnerships, Product Marketing, Communications, Legal, and partner teams. Build relationships that unlock strong stories. Work directly with partner founders, executives, marketing teams, and customers to uncover differentiated outcomes and move opportunities from initial conversation through publication. Prioritize for business impact. Focus resources on opportunities that support adoption, qualified pipeline, and partner growth, balancing near-term opportunities with the long-term development of the reference program. Put content to work across channels. Partner with Sales, Field Marketing, and campaign teams to bring customer proof into sales conversations, partner programs, campaigns, events, and digital experiences. Create an effective operating rhythm. Maintain a clear editorial pipeline, ownership, approval process, and publishing cadence. Track reference readiness, content engagement, sales usage, and contribution to pipeline and adoption, using those insights to improve the program. You might thrive in this role if you have: 10+ years of experience across partner marketing, product marketing, customer marketing, content marketing, communications, or related B2B technology marketing roles. Exceptional storytelling and editorial judgment, with the ability to absorb substantial information quickly and turn it into a coherent narrative, strategy, and message. Experience building customer reference or storytelling programs, including developing case studies, whitepapers, webinars, and thought leadership grounded in credible customer outcomes. Strong business judgment and a track record of choosing marketing investments based on customer relevance, pipeline potential, adoption, and commercial impact. A hands-on approach to execution. You are comfortable conducting interviews, drafting content, developing messaging, coordinating approvals, and getting work published. Strong relationship-building skills, curiosity, and persistence. You can earn trust with founders, executives, and customers, ask thoughtful questions, and follow through to bring stories to completion. The ability to collaborate across Partnerships, Sales, Product Marketing, Communications, Brand, and Legal while maintaining clear ownership and momentum. Experience translating technical capabilities into accessible customer value, with careful attention to accuracy, substantiation, and permissions. Comfort moving between strategy and execution, building an initial version quickly, learning from results, and creating repeatable programs that scale.
